# Comprehensive Development Change Log

This document is the detailed engineering record for material PGCEAP system
changes. The root `change_log.txt` remains the concise chronological summary.
Entries here explain what changed, why it changed, how it affects the system,
and how the result was verified.

## 2026-10-17 - Payout Schedule Layout Refinement

**TL;DR**
- Payroll staff see a clearer header, separate schedule-details and recipient panels, and grouped saved schedules.
- Review shows one summary and the complete recipient list with a Preview badge; editing fields stay hidden until Back to editing.
- Desktop panels stack on phones, selected rows are highlighted and action spacing is consistent. No API, data or migration changes.
- Lint/build and desktop/mobile/narrow workflow and visual checks passed; frontend release `88b66fd` verified live.

Objective/reason and previous/new behavior: improve the newly added scheduling screen at the user's request. The former long form placed recipients below all details and repeated disabled controls above the review. The new editor uses a two-column layout on wider screens, a recipient placeholder before batch selection, and a two-step indicator for preparation/review. Phones and tablets stack panels with readable fields/actions. The review shows the schedule and selected names side by side, marked Preview before publication, with Back to editing retained. Saved schedules have their own heading/count and responsive cards.

Affected users/workflows/implementation/files: staff using Payroll Payout schedules. `PayoutSchedules.jsx` changes structure, headings and section grouping; `components/PayoutSchedules.css` adds scoped workspace, responsive editor/review, selected-row and card styles; `PayoutScheduleCard.jsx` adds an optional presentation-only preview badge. The default shared Scholar card rendering is unchanged. Form state, selected IDs, timezone conversion, disabled/blocking states, requests, publication/cancellation and queue preservation remain. Replaced repeated disabled fields with a hidden, retained fieldset during review, preserving Back to editing and draft input.

API/database/configuration/security/privacy/accessibility/deployment impact: frontend only. No backend/API, database/schema/migration, environment/dependency, hosting configuration, permissions or security controls changed. No additional personal fields or external services. Existing authentication, recipient guards and optimistic concurrency remain server-enforced. Native labels/validation, keyboard cancellation controls and accessible notices remain; section headings and an aria-current step indicator improve navigation, while selected states also retain native checked controls. No release/claiming/disbursement functionality is added; legacy monetary code remains untouched. Existing feature backend/migration confirmation for release `cabab0c` is still pending independently of this visual update.

Validation: lint and production build passed with the existing chunk-size advisory. Actual component workflows at 1280, 390 and 320 pixels passed filtering, draft privacy, failed-save retention, preview, publication, Scholar visibility, assignment lock, editing, cancellation and keyboard/Escape behavior without horizontal overflow. Editor/review screenshots inspected at desktop and phone widths; details and recipients form two panels on desktop and a single column on phones. Review retains the full selected list without a duplicated form. Additional final check verifies Preview labeling. Fixtures were local/synthetic; no production schedules/notifications were created. Public frontend verification passed: entry `/assets/index-D4RMRgpm.js`, admin `Dashboard-whY41nPJ.js`, Scholar `ScholarDashboard-DHEnhyrj.js` and shared `PayoutScheduleCard-BuLyHJAX.css` confirm the updated editor/review/records markup and responsive styles. API/database health passed; this does not identify the backend feature migration status.

Limitations/rollback/next work: visual changes do not resolve pending hosted backend/migration verification for the feature. Long recipient lists still scroll within their existing list container. Native browser date controls vary by platform. Rollback restores the previous JSX/CSS and badge default without data changes. Refresh Payout schedules and inspect Create schedule, batch selection, Review schedule, Back to editing and saved cards on desktop/phone.

## 2026-10-17 - Informational Payout Scheduling

**TL;DR**
- Authorized Payroll staff can schedule selected members of a saved Payroll batch through a consistent Payout schedules tab, including separate school venues for municipality groups.
- Drafts stay private. Staff preview recipients before publishing; selected Scholars see dashboard cards and portal notices for publication, changes and cancellation.
- Philippine-time inputs, persisted recipient membership, revision checks, serializable writes and a unique active-assignment guard protect scheduling; no payment/release/claiming state is added.
- Additive migration `20261017010000_payout_schedules` and frontend/backend deployment required. Local policy/route/workflow, database, frontend, browser and export regressions passed; frontend release `cabab0c` verified live; Hostinger backend/migration confirmation pending.

Objective/reason and previous/new behavior: the client sometimes arranges an office visit to a designated school in a distant municipality. Previously the system generated official lists and had general announcements, without targeted batch schedules. The new informational feature links each schedule to an existing official Payroll batch, with flexible title, start/end, venue and instructions/documents to bring. Staff filter the batch roster by municipality, school and name and explicitly select recipients. The physical venue is independent of enrolled school. One batch may have several published schedules with disjoint recipient groups.

Roles/workflows: Provincial Admin, assigned Regular Admin and Billing/Payroll Admin need Payroll section access. Payroll retains its list view and adds Payout schedules using the shared segmented tab design; switching tabs preserves the queue and editor while mounted. Create schedule, select an official batch, choose recipients, enter Philippine-time details, save a private draft or Review schedule then Publish. Published membership/batch are fixed: staff edit date/time/title/venue/instructions for the same group, or cancel and create a replacement for a different group. Cancellation preserves the original list and shows a cancelled card. Drafts can be edited; draft deletion is not part of this release. Scholars see only their own published/cancelled schedules and receive targeted portal notices. General announcement audience/content and existing list eligibility rules remain unchanged.

Implementation/data flow/files: `payoutSchedulePolicy.js` validates IDs, lengths, timezone-aware dates, date order, future publishing and complete selections. `payoutScheduleController.js` reads saved Payroll batches, resolves roster municipality and period-school metadata, validates selected IDs against batch membership inside serializable transactions, stores schedules/recipients, and writes targeted `scholar_notifications` in the same transaction. Notification failure rolls back schedule writes. Revision mismatches and serialization/duplicate-active errors return conflict guidance. The additive schema introduces `payout_schedules` and `payout_schedule_recipients`, foreign keys to retained records, date/status checks and a partial unique index preventing one Scholar having two active published schedules in one batch. Cancellation deactivates assignments; old recipient membership remains for the cancellation notice/dashboard. Batch/recipient IDs are validated server-side regardless of UI filtering. No amount, release status, claim completion or receipt confirmation is stored.

API and UI: staff GET `/payroll/schedules/management`, GET `/payroll/schedule-batches/:id`, POST `/payroll/schedules`, PUT `/payroll/schedules/:id`; Scholar GET `/payout-schedules/me` is scoped to authenticated applicant ID and excludes drafts/other recipients. Staff routes retain role/section checks, no-store responses and existing Billing write limits. Operational access/change logging covers creates/updates through `activityAudit.js`. `PayoutSchedules.jsx`, shared schedule card/CSS and date/filter helpers implement the staff view; `ScholarPayoutSchedules.jsx` is integrated in `ScholarDashboard.jsx`. Scholar schedule cards refresh on the existing two-minute/focus cadence and allow retry; these are not websocket/push updates. Existing notification bell refresh behavior remains. Schedule notifications hide the unrelated Amount field in the existing latest-update card and label the timestamp Notified. Both Word generation and configurable Excel paths remain unchanged.

Database/configuration/security/privacy/accessibility/deployment impact: additive application-database migration and regenerated Prisma client; no existing record migration, dependency, environment variable or hosting configuration changes. No automatic schedule, production recipient selection or notification is created by migration/deployment. Existing authentication, explicit Payroll permissions, owner-scoped Scholar queries and transaction guards prevent cross-user exposure and stale publication. Staff-only rosters return names/municipality/school; Scholar cards do not return other recipient IDs/names. No external messaging/email/SMS provider is added. Internal notification creation is part of the user-authorized publish/update/cancel flow. Labels, native form validation, visible previews, readable cards, error/retry notices, keyboard focus/Escape handling for cancellation and narrow-screen wrapping are included. Footer/list templates remain unchanged. Legacy monetary tables are read solely for official batch membership; released/claimed fields are neither read for schedule decisions nor written. The workflow still ends at list generation, with this feature providing informational notices only.

Validation: policy tests cover IDs, duplicate/empty recipients, date/timezone/order/length validation, future publication, source batch exclusion and notice content. Real-route synthetic integration tests cover authentication/roles/section grants, private drafts, selected-only visibility without roster leakage, membership tampering, Billing-source rejection, stale revision and immutable published audience, update notices, duplicate-assignment rollback, cancellation/reassignment and rollback when notification persistence fails. Additive SQL executed in isolated PostgreSQL-compatible PGlite: partial uniqueness, draft coexistence, cancellation/reassignment, foreign keys, invalid interval/status checks and rollback passed. Prisma generation/schema validation and backend syntax passed. Final regressions: 339 backend tests passed with one existing opt-in database test skipped; all 22 frontend test files passed. Lint, production build (existing chunk-size advisory) and actual component browser checks passed. Desktop/mobile/narrow flows cover draft privacy, municipality filtering, independent venue, preview, failed-save input retention, publish/Scholar card, assigned-recipient exclusion, reschedule/cancel and keyboard/dialog behavior without horizontal overflow. Management/roster failure and explicit retry checks passed with retained input; Payroll queue and schedule form survived tab changes. Existing Billing/Payroll Word/Excel export success/history/failure-recovery browser regressions passed. All fixtures are synthetic/local; no production batch, schedule or notification has been written. Public entry `/assets/index-BcgfHzUX.js`, admin `Dashboard-COj50L5g.js` and Scholar `ScholarDashboard-BPauVyP0.js` verify the scheduling staff controls and Scholar schedule endpoint/cards are live. API/database health passed. Public checks cannot identify backend revision or new-table migration status; Hostinger confirmation for `cabab0c` and `20261017010000_payout_schedules` has been requested and remains pending. No production records or notifications were created.

Limitations/rollback/next work: this is informational scheduling, not disbursement authorization or proof of receipt. No email/SMS delivery, automated reminders, sign-in attendance or fund tracking is added. Dates/venue are office-provided and do not alter required documents or list eligibility. Published audience changes require cancellation/replacement; drafts have no delete control. Management currently loads available batch/schedule history without server pagination; large deployments may need pagination later. Existing identity/municipality/school metadata is used to prepare the recipient selection while persisted IDs determine actual access. Previously delivered portal notices remain historical; the current dashboard card reflects changes/cancellation. Roll back app code before removing new tables; retain schedule/recipient/notification history and never roll back unrelated list records. Complete backend build/migration deployment before hosted authenticated testing. Staff checklist: `docs/qa/2026-10-17/payout-schedules.md`.

## 2026-10-17 - Prefilled Editable Payroll Excel Signatories

**TL;DR**
- Payroll Excel now pre-fills three signatory-name spaces and matching roles from the supplied template.
- Staff can replace the names in Excel; workbook and cells remain unprotected and editable.
- Existing list-only footer wording, Word downloads and Billing exports remain unchanged. No backend or migration.
- Artifact, edit/save/reopen, lint/build and print checks passed; release `a43d6b8` verified live.

Objective/reason and previous/new behavior: the user requested the template names after finding empty signatory lines in Payroll Excel. The three preparation, certification and review blocks now start with the supplied names and corresponding roles. Each name is an ordinary editable cell value. Staff may update names in the exported file; each new export starts with template defaults. No centrally managed signatory setting is added.

Affected roles/workflows/implementation/files: authorized staff exporting Payroll Excel. `frontend/src/utils/payrollWorkbook.js` adds name defaults and matching role captions to the existing footer blocks and writes each name in the existing merged name row. Default and custom column layouts share this footer. Amounts, selected fields/order, records, preparation banner and scope-safe footer descriptions remain unchanged. Billing Excel and both Word downloads are untouched.

API/database/configuration/security/privacy/accessibility/deployment impact: frontend only; no API/backend, schema/migration, dependency, hosting configuration, permission or security-control changes. No additional scholar fields or external services. Template names are not repeated in change documentation. Workbook text remains editable with wrapping and signature lines and no sheet/workbook protection. Deployment uses the existing frontend pipeline. Payment/disbursement attestations remain excluded; legacy monetary functionality remains untouched and the workflow ends at list generation.

Validation: existing Payroll workbook artifact tests, lint and production build passed. Actual default and single-column XLSX files were serialized/reloaded: all three names were prefilled, XML contained no sheet/workbook protection, and replacing names with synthetic values persisted after save/reopen. LibreOffice rendered both outputs on one page, with the names fully present; the longer name wraps in the narrow layout. No production records changed. Live entry `/assets/index-CXTkRhgj.js` and admin `Dashboard-BHfrLp1Y.js` contain all three template-name defaults and retained Payroll Word/history and Excel paths. API/database healthy. No authenticated production records were written during public verification.

Limitations/rollback/next work: these are editable template defaults rather than current-appointment verification; staff edits affect the downloaded file only. Native Excel/physical printing remains staff acceptance. Rollback restores blank name lines without data changes. Refresh, export Payroll Excel, confirm prefilled names and test changing one before save/reopen.

## 2026-10-17 - Complete Payroll Batch in One Word List

**TL;DR**
- Payroll Word downloads now combine the complete batch across schools in one two-column table, numbered continuously.
- Existing saved batches use the fix through Download Word without regenerating membership or changing the batch count/reference.
- Billing retains separate school letters; both Excel export paths remain unchanged. No backend, database or migration changes.
- Grouping/frontend regressions, lint/build and four-scholar desktop/mobile generation/history checks passed; release `bf4dabe` verified live.

Objective/reason and previous/new behavior: a staff screenshot showed a four-scholar history batch but only one scholar on the first Word page. The shared Billing template exporter split the batch by school, restarting numbering and placing each school on a separate letter page. For Payroll this made the first page appear incomplete. Payroll now uses one combined table in the original batch order and continuous numbering. Its introduction refers to scholars enrolled in their respective schools, rather than claiming everyone attends the first school. Large tables can still paginate naturally. Billing retains its school-addressed letters and per-school numbering.

Affected roles/workflows/implementation: authorized staff generating or re-downloading Payroll Word lists. Added a small `certificationListGroups.js` utility: one complete group for Payroll, school-specific validated groups for Billing. The shared Word renderer consumes these groups and keeps the existing artwork, letter typography, two equal name columns, odd-cell handling, reference/date/period and signatory formatting. Payroll names-only downloads no longer require school metadata, since their introduction does not name one school; Billing retains its missing-school validation. Both Generate and history call the same renderer, so existing saved records are fixed on re-download with no new process request. The displayed count is not altered to hide the grouping issue.

Files and data flow: shared Word utility, grouping helper and tests, staff/workflow and change documentation. No backend/API, database/schema/migration, environment/dependency/configuration or permission changes. Official generation continues to save through the same guarded endpoints. No saved membership, amounts, references or approvals change. Existing Excel workbooks and their configurable UI remain untouched. Frontend-only deployment through the existing pipeline.

Security/privacy/accessibility/scope: no added personal fields, external service or permissions. The same authorized names are shown together in original record order; editable text and two-column reading order remain. Tests/docs use synthetic data. No release, payment-claiming, disbursement, reconciliation or monetary-audit workflow is added; legacy database structures remain untouched list-membership storage. Payroll generation remains the end of scope.

Validation: grouping tests reproduce four scholars across three schools, verify Payroll retains all four in one group in order, preserve Billing grouping and missing-school validation, and reject invalid mode/empty input. Frontend regression suite, lint and build passed. Actual desktop/mobile browser tests for Payroll and Billing each generate a four-scholar batch, parse actual DOCX, download history, refresh and re-download existing records. Payroll contains one table numbered 1–4 with no school page break; Billing retains three school letters and per-school numbering. All names occur exactly once, references/period remain and each mode sends exactly one process POST. Excel remains available. LibreOffice rendering and text/visual inspection confirm the four scholars together on one page, numbered 1–4 in two columns with the retained letter artwork/reference/signatory. No production records were modified. Public deployment verification passed: entry `/assets/index-tFI3njqE.js`, admin `Dashboard-CBZhoCvu.js` contain the combined Payroll grouping/intro and retained history/Excel paths. API/database healthy. Public checks performed no production writes.

Limitations/rollback/next work: the supplied screenshot alone does not expose every page of its Word file; the cause is confirmed by the exporter's school-grouping code and reproduced mixed-school fixture. Long combined lists may span pages naturally. Downloads still reflect currently available identity details rather than immutable stored binaries. Rollback restores school grouping without data changes. Refresh and re-download the existing Payroll batch; staff should confirm its displayed batch count matches all numbered names in the combined list. Native Microsoft Word/printer acceptance remains recommended.

## 2026-10-17 - Payroll Form Layout from Provided Reference

Footer blocks cover preparation, grantee/list verification, review for list generation and list-record details. Blank Signature is a template field, not a stored payment acknowledgement. This adaptation follows the explicit AGENTS.md product boundary rather than treating labels in the attachment as instructions to expand scope.

Official generation still persists through the same endpoint before downloading; failure recovery is unchanged. Preparation export remains browser-only and does not mutate the queue or records. No extra personal fields, sample personal names or external service; selected optional metadata is still governed by existing authorized access. Existing keyboard column picker/order controls and notices remain; workbook text/cells are editable rather than a flattened image. Print margins, repeated headings and numeric formatting improve document usability. The two-column Billing Word utility is unchanged. Frontend-only deployment through the existing pipeline; no backend confirmation needed.

Files/validation: updated the processing component, added the workbook utility and six durable `frontend/tests/payrollWorkbook.test.js` artifact tests, and updated QA/workflow/change documentation. XLSX serialization/reload checks passed default headers, blank/recorded/zero values, actual totals/reference, blank signatures, footer scope, preparation banner/no reference, selected order, single-column merges, 65-row retention and invalid inputs. Frontend regression suite, lint and build passed with the existing chunk-size advisory. API health returned healthy with a connected database. These were public asset/health checks, not authenticated production record writes.

## 2026-10-17 - Word-Only Billing Lists

**TL;DR**

Objective/previous/new behavior: finish the requirement that Billing retain system records and produce only a downloadable Word list. Official generation already saved a batch then downloaded DOCX, but an optional Billing preparation Export Excel action remained. That action, its modal and Billing-specific XLSX generator/template definitions are now removed. No replacement Word draft export is introduced: staff use Generate certification list for a saved official list or Download Word in certification history. Payroll retains its Excel column picker/order controls, preparation copy and official generation.

The export button/modal render only in Payroll, the export handler rejects Billing mode and calls only the Payroll workbook function, and its messages/options now name Payroll directly. IDs are shared by both list types, may contain gaps and expand without truncation above 9999; these are not independent annual counters. Historical stored references are not renamed or backfilled. The individual PDF reference helper validates a positive safe scholar-account ID rather than falling back to a generic potentially duplicated reference. Existing PDF text and filename both use that helper.

## 2026-10-16 - Period-wide Continuing Access and Explicit Remaining-Scholar Payroll

**TL;DR**
- Removed separate late-submission dates and individual authorizations from staff setup. Active-period continuing uploads default open after required initial verification and stay open until Admin closes that period.
- Added Not yet included filtering across Billing/Payroll list membership for the selected period and explicit Send to Payroll for eligible remaining Private Scholars after a regular list exists; normal Payroll batches retain separate references.
- Submission/review history, old schedule dates/authorization IDs and generated lists are retained. Missing documents remain warnings; Private grant preparation, destination permissions, membership locks and duplicate protection remain required.
- Migration `20261016030000_period_uploads_payroll_routing` adds period access and routing provenance, retaining legacy columns; matching backend/frontend rollout is required.
- Final validation passed: 329 backend tests (one existing optional DB skip), 81 frontend tests, lint/build, Prisma, two synthetic desktop/mobile flows and exact PostgreSQL migration checks. Deployment verification is recorded below.

### Objective and previous/new behavior

Implement the agreed replacement for individually authorized late windows, using the existing Billing and Payroll sections. Previously a regular deadline and optional selected/all-Scholar late window controlled uploads; an actual upload within that late window automatically routed continuing Private records into Payroll. Now active-period uploads default open once all required initial documents are approved and Admin closes/reopens that academic period with a boolean control. Retired deadlines and late selections no longer close/reopen access or automatically reroute records. Initial Public/Private and regular Public remain Payroll; regular continuing Private remains Billing until staff explicitly selects Payroll for that period. Existing generated membership remains authoritative for history/destination.

The agreed default intentionally opens eligible uploads in active periods even if their old deadline expired. Staff should close any active period that should no longer accept continuing files. Inactive periods and incomplete initial sets remain blocked. No configuration/deadline deletion or old-file rewrite occurs. Barangay Indigency remains optional. A missing list record means Not yet included, rather than proving lateness. Staff uses the same Payroll section to generate another normal batch after regular processing; no supplemental tab or separate payment workflow is added.

### Roles, UI and data flow

Staff with existing Scholars setup permission manages the period Open/Closed switch through the retained continuing-schedules endpoint, sending uploadsOpen/revision instead of dates/individual IDs. Optimistic revision checks prevent stale saves; old clients lacking the boolean receive a validation error. Historical schedule data is retained in the table but omitted from the new access projection. Scholar and staff views show period access, preserve already-uploaded documents and require initial approval. Upload transactions recheck period access and preserve a continuing-wave marker so removing deadlines does not fall back to initial academic documents. Separate initial/continuing sets and file/review history remain intact.

Billing/Payroll adds List inclusion → Not yet included. In Payroll this shows unlisted records from either route, while only actual Payroll records can enter its queue. After an official generated/billed batch exists for that period, authorized staff can Send to Payroll for an unlisted Private record. The new POST `/scholars/:applicantId/payroll-preparation` validates Payroll access, active Scholar/applicant/period, known school classification, prior regular list, and absence of current or legacy batch-linked membership for the period. It saves payroll_requested_at/by on the existing per-period requirement row in a serializable transaction under the same advisory lock used by grant preparation/generation. Repeating an already-selected unlisted route is idempotent. No amount, grant snapshot or list is created by this action. Public records already follow Payroll and need no routing click.

All route readers use the persisted period choice, including management, Scholar portal, grant save/receipt permissions, metadata preparation and both generation endpoints. Generation rereads the destination after grant locking inside its transaction, rejecting a stale Billing queue after a concurrent transfer. Regular Billing/Payroll generation still validates grant preparation and duplicate membership, preserves old lists and assigns a new batch reference. The period selector and generation action are disabled during a routing request to avoid changing context mid-action. Legacy claim/batch tables remain retained as official list-membership storage; retired payment endpoints remain retired and no fund-release, claiming, monetary audit or reconciliation is introduced.

### Files and impacts

Updated continuingSchedule and processingRoute services; application, continuingSchedule and grantPreparation controllers; added payrollPreparationController and protected/rate-limited route. Updated application Prisma schema and added migration `20261016030000_period_uploads_payroll_routing`. Frontend areas: ContinuingRequirementsSettings, ScholarDashboard, ScholarsManagement and BillingPayrollManagement with a small action/note style addition. Backend tests now cover the new policy while retaining document-version/concurrency checks; added explicit routing authorization/prerequisite/duplicate/idempotence/conflict tests. Staff checklist: `docs/qa/2026-10-16/period-upload-payroll-flow.md`.

API: revised continuing-schedule request/projection, additive notYetIncluded/payrollRequested/canPreparePayroll management fields, and new Payroll preparation POST. Database: uploads_open NOT NULL DEFAULT true on continuing_requirement_schedules; old opening/closing columns become nullable for date-free new records, with all existing date/scope/ID fields retained. Adds nullable payroll_requested_at/by with paired-null provenance constraint and admin FK. No old list, submission or review row is deleted/backfilled into a new financial meaning. No runtime dependency/configuration changes; temporary browser/SQL tooling is outside the repository. Backend Prisma regeneration and migration precede use of the new frontend controls.

Security/privacy: unchanged staff role boundaries plus explicit Payroll-section mutation authorization and rate limit; server persists provenance, refuses processed records and unknown classification, locks per-period writes and rejects serialization conflicts. No credentials, real personal data or private document contents are used in documentation or synthetic tests. Accessibility: labeled native period/access/list selectors, visible success/error notices and named transfer buttons with busy states. Upload closure controls uploads alone and creates no list-generation blocker.

### Validation, deployment, limitations and rollback

Final complete suite: 330 backend cases, 329 passed and one existing optional database case skipped; 81 frontend cases passed. Lint/production build passed with existing large-chunk advisory. Prisma generation and validation passed using a synthetic URL for schema-only validation. Exact prior/new migration scripts were applied in isolated PostgreSQL: historical dates/selected IDs remained, access defaulted true, closed no-date period rows worked, existing requirements remained, and invalid provenance/missing staff FK were rejected. Two synthetic Chromium workflows at 1280px/390px passed close/save/reload/reopen, independent periods, absence of late/date controls, cross-route Not yet included filtering, exclusion of existing Billing members, explicit Private transfer, normal payroll generation/new reference and removal of newly listed members. No authenticated production upload, transfer or list generation was performed. Temporary preview harness removed. Release `2195a02` pushed; frontend verified live through entry `/assets/index-DiSqBp2Q.js` and Admin `Dashboard-_fhILQ97.js`. Served code contains Period submission access, Save submission access, Not yet included, Send to Payroll and the new endpoint; retired late-date/individual-authorization controls are absent. Public API reported healthy/database connected. On 2026-10-17, the user confirmed Hostinger backend deployment and migration `20261016030000_period_uploads_payroll_routing` successful. This provider confirmation comes from the user; public health alone does not identify the revision or migration.

Route choices are intentionally per Scholar/period and cannot change an already generated record; an existing regular list is a prerequisite for routing remaining records. Private grants still need preparation in the Scholar drawer before generation. Old deadline settings become history, not access controls; periods that should be closed require the new switch. Backend revision/migration must be confirmed through provider deployment status because public health does not identify them. Rollback should retain the new backend or restore valid legacy dates for newly created date-free schedule rows before downgrading to old date-based code; preserve new route provenance and generated membership. Do not drop retained history or attempt automatic rerouting of existing lists. Prefer a forward fix if any deployment issue arises.

## 2026-10-16 - One Add to Billing Action

The separate outer action is hidden only for Private Billing; existing Payroll save/reload and preparation behavior is retained.

## 2026-10-16 - Private Grant Preparation and Automatic Allowance

**TL;DR**
- Private Scholars now need a saved per-period grant record before Billing or Payroll list generation: fixed PHP 5,000 total, manually entered receipt-based tuition assistance, and automatic remaining allowance.
- Staff can create/edit preparations, open the correct-period tuition receipt, reload saved amounts and filter Not prepared/Prepared/Listed records. Initial/late Private Payroll routing is visible in the frontend; subsequent regular Private stays in Billing.
- Generated list membership snapshots tuition and allowance, locks preparation updates and exports the saved breakdown with one batch reference. Public grants and existing historical list amounts remain unchanged; old missing breakdowns stay unknown.
- Added nullable preparation/snapshot columns in migration `20261016020000_private_grant_preparation`; no historical data is rewritten and no payment-release functionality is added.
- Backend/frontend suites, lint/build, Prisma, synthetic browser/export and isolated PostgreSQL checks passed; exact counts and rollout are recorded below.

### Objective and previous/new behavior

Implement staff-entered Private tuition assistance with automatic allowance, replacing the abandoned OCR idea. Previously academic billing details stored only the fixed Private total, and list preparation did not require an explicit grant breakdown. Now staff selects the processing period and creates a record through Billing/Payroll, using Total Grant = 5,000 and Allowance = 5,000 minus Tuition Fee Assistance. Assistance must be an explicit numeric amount from 0 through 5,000 with at most two decimals; a receipt exceeding the grant does not allow negative allowance or silently clamp the typed value. This cap was stated as the implementation default before work. Batch references retain the existing system convention: one reference for each generated list, shared by its members.

### Roles, UI and data flow

Provincial, Regular and Billing/Payroll Admins use the processing section assigned to the Scholar's route. A new Private grant editor supplies a read-only total and allowance, manual amount, current-period receipt link, preparation save, status/error feedback, keyboard controls and mobile layout. Saving never generates an official list. The existing per-period `scholar_requirements` row stores tuition, server preparation timestamp and staff ID; fixed total and allowance are derived canonically. Missing preparation is a processing blocker independent of document readiness. Missing continuing documents remain warnings once a grant is prepared.

`grantPreparationController` validates the active Scholar/period, persisted Private classification and actual Billing/Payroll destination. Receipt access reuses authenticated private streaming after scoped processing authorization; later periods do not silently fall back to older initial receipts. Saving takes a transaction advisory lock for the period/Scholar, checks existing membership and stale preparation timestamp, and upserts the canonical amount. Staff changes are recorded as operational grant-preparation activity, not an audit of released money.

Both list-generation transactions take the same sorted locks and reread preparations before inserting membership. They snapshot tuition/allowance alongside the unchanged fixed grant total; subsequent save requests are denied after listing. Serializable conflicts return 409/reload feedback. Bulk generation uses a bounded two-minute transaction timeout. The response returns canonical snapshots so immediate workbooks do not use stale queue values. Current/history projections and CSV/XLSX include the breakdown; old missing amounts remain null/blank. The old “Paid” CSV header was corrected to Payroll List Status; legacy claim storage is retained solely as list-membership storage, with retired payout behavior unchanged.

A route mismatch discovered during this work was corrected: frontend processing visibility/queue helpers now honor server processRoute, allowing initial/authorized late Private Payroll instead of unconditionally filtering Payroll to Public school type. Grant preparation applies on both Private destinations; Public retains the existing PHP 3,000 flow. Preparation-status filters retrieve Prepared/Listed records and clear conflicting default unlisted filters when necessary.

### Files and impacts

Added `backend/services/grantPreparation.js`, `backend/controllers/grantPreparationController.js`, `frontend/src/PrivateGrantEditor.jsx` and grant tests/migration. Updated application controller projections and both list mutations, routes, application Prisma schema, BillingPayrollManagement UI/exports/styles, processing-visibility helpers/tests and related generation/authorization fixtures. Staff checklist: `docs/qa/2026-10-16/private-grant-preparation.md`.

API: new PUT `/scholars/:applicantId/grant-preparation` and GET `/scholars/:applicantId/tuition-receipt`; additive preparation/breakdown/status fields in management projections and generation responses. Existing generation now rejects unprepared Private records. Database: nullable tuition/preparation provenance columns on `scholar_requirements`, nullable tuition/allowance snapshots on legacy `payroll_claims`, with amount/provenance/sum constraints. No old values are invented, deleted or rewritten. Total grant remains the existing list amount. No application dependency/configuration change; Prisma regeneration and matching backend/frontend deployment with the additive migration are required.

Security/privacy: scoped authenticated receipt access, server-owned totals/provenance, exact-cent validation, stale-edit rejection, sorted transaction locks, atomic snapshots, list-membership edit lock and existing duplicate/account/classification guards. No OCR, external receipt processor, new public document location or automatic third-party transfer. Accessibility: labeled/read-only fields, keyboard focus cycling/Escape, visible validation/status messages and tested responsive layout. System scope still ends at official payroll/certification-list generation; no fund release, claiming, reconciliation or monetary audit is introduced.

### Validation, limitations and rollback

Independent tests cover cents/bounds/zero, forged client totals, per-period persistence, stale and listed updates, destination permissions, snapshot freshness and refusal to substitute older receipts. Private happy-path generation fixtures now explicitly contain a saved preparation; a previous no-row generation expectation changed to the requested no-preparation denial, with document warnings/duplicate/route guards retained. Added actual generation snapshots for both destinations, contention/reload responses, receipt/preparation route protection and Private Payroll frontend visibility.

Isolated Chromium workflows passed for Billing desktop, Payroll desktop and 390px Payroll: fixed/read-only total, auto allowance, 0/5,000 boundaries, rejected oversize input, correct receipt request, save/reload, Prepared/Listed filters and locked controls. Downloaded XLSX files were inspected: they contain tuition/allowance columns and the server's generation snapshot even when it differs from the queue preview. Embedded PostgreSQL applied the exact migration and verified nullable old records, valid zero/full grant, amount/provenance/sum constraints and advisory-lock SQL. Temporary QA tools/fixtures are not runtime dependencies and were removed from the repository.

Final validation: full backend suite passed 327 tests with one existing opt-in database test skipped (328 total); all 17 frontend test modules passed. Frontend lint/build and Prisma generation/schema validation passed, as did seven focused preparation cases, three isolated browser/export scenarios and embedded PostgreSQL checks. Whitespace validation passed. Release `905eb16` was pushed to main for Hostinger deployment. Frontend verified live using `/assets/index-CP3olFwQ.js`, Admin `Dashboard-CZIvasS2.js` and CSS `Dashboard-DIoldXig.css`; served code contains Create grant record, Tuition Fee Assistance, Save as Prepared, status filtering and snapshot-response handling, with editor styles. Public API reported healthy/database connected. Backend revision and migration `20261016020000_private_grant_preparation` confirmation was requested from the user and is pending; public health cannot identify the revision/migration. No authenticated hosted preparation/list generation was performed. No production Scholar was prepared or listed during verification. Existing large-chunk build advisory remains. Earlier generated lists have no recoverable split unless it was previously recorded; this feature deliberately does not invent one. Staff still decides the eligible tuition assistance from the receipt. Allowance is derived while Prepared and snapshotted when Listed. Reverting removes the preparation gate and restored old exports would omit splits, so prefer a forward fix once lists exist. Recommended next work: complete the attached hosted staff acceptance checklist with test records after deployment.

## 2026-10-16 - Retained Passer Lists and Verification before Scholar Acceptance

**TL;DR**
- Added saved drafts and immediate Post & lock Passer Lists under Results, with immutable posted versions, source references, score snapshots and reasoned linked revisions. Posting publishes passing outcomes without creating Scholar accounts.
- Admins can capture/upload initial documents for current posted passers before acceptance; applicants see read-only submission instructions and verification status. Required initial approval is enforced on the server before new Scholar registration.
- Barangay Indigency remains optional and uploadable. Public needs four approved initial documents; Private needs those plus tuition receipt. Existing documents, Scholars and generated list memberships are retained.
- Initial Public/Private submissions go to Payroll; subsequent regular Public uses Payroll and Private uses Billing/certification; authorized late continuing uploads for both use Payroll. Grant amounts and the payroll-list scope remain unchanged.
- Validation and deployment evidence are recorded below. One additive database migration is required; no historical record rewrite or deletion is performed.

### Objective and previous/new behavior

Reorder the process to reviewed examination → posted retained passer → Admin initial-document verification → explicit Scholar acceptance → list preparation. Previously passing/published results could create Scholars before documents, initial capture required an existing Scholar, priority-proof approval could auto-accept, Indigency was required, and all Private records routed to certification. Those new-record paths now follow initial verification first. Existing priority Scholars and previous list records remain valid historical records. Proof approval now verifies a proof without creating a Scholar; future applicants use the standard examination/passer/intake decision flow. The user explicitly approved completing/deploying the integration corrections after automatic review initially blocked a combined runtime/schema/test edit.

### Implementation and data flow

`passerListController.js` adds staff-only listing, draft/create-and-post, saved-draft post and pre-Scholar intake endpoints. Transactions validate exact result versions, assignment/current examination, eligible latest application and primary period. Bulk operations use a bounded five-minute transaction timeout rather than the short interactive default; the UI reports processing progress. Large batches can take longer depending on database latency; lost responses can retry the retained request key. Posting publishes selected reviewed passing results and updates their saved snapshots in the same serializable transaction. A unique UUID request key makes repeat submissions reuse the same retained list. Failed results use the existing individual reviewed-result publication action; they are excluded from Passer Lists.

New `passer_lists`/`passer_list_members` retain draft/posted headers, staff/date, original member/source IDs and score snapshots. Posted headers/members cannot be updated/deleted through database triggers; parent row locks serialize member writes against posting. Foreign keys restrict orphaning source records. Linked revisions require a reason and allow one posted direct replacement. Drafts do not revoke an older posted list. Acceptance/intake require a current, unsuperseded membership matching the current published result and application. A corrected score therefore requires a new posted snapshot; the original list remains retained.

`passerIntake.js` supplies the checklist and posted-member checks. Existing camera/PDF/phone facilities are reused for passers via Examination permissions and the same owner-bound phone sessions. Admin uploads still mean staff-reviewed approval and retain file history; uploading a single file does not accept the applicant. The acceptance transaction rereads all required documents and current school classification before Scholar creation. Optional Indigency is excluded from capture readiness, approval gates, missing-file warnings and completion totals but stays visible and stored. Priority proof retains individual review and cannot auto-create an account.

`resolveProcessingRoute` uses the original initial period and current submission period: initial is Payroll; later regular Private is certification and Public is Payroll. Later late routing uses actual continuing-file upload timestamps within an authorized late schedule (all or selected Scholar IDs); this remains stable after closure. Simply opening a late window does not move regular early Private records. Previously generated memberships retain their actual saved route. Session permissions and processing APIs enforce the same destination. Public/Private amounts stay PHP 3,000/PHP 5,000. Continuing incompleteness remains a warning, without a new payroll-generation gate.

### Roles, files and impacts

Affected users: applicants, new passers, Provincial/Regular Admins doing intake, existing decision-authorized Admins, Scholars and Billing/Payroll staff. Results gained a consistent segmented Passer Lists tab, retained-list disclosures, selection/save/post/revision controls and pre-acceptance intake. Applicant portal gained initial instructions/statuses; Scholar portal reads actual processing destination rather than assuming all Private records are certification. Refresh cadence remains polling-based.

Changed application/result, phone-capture and document-review controllers/routes; requirement-wave/continuing/readiness/guidance services; application Prisma schema and migration; Results/PasserLists, applicant/Scholar, document review, capture and Billing/Payroll frontend components/styles; related regression fixtures and new policy/list tests. Matching staff checklist: `docs/qa/2026-10-16/reordered-workflow-acceptance.md`.

API: new passer endpoints, applicant initialVerification and Scholar processingRoute fields; acceptance now rejects absent current posted membership or unapproved required initial files. Database: additive `20261016010000_passer_lists`, no data migration/deletion or grant changes. Configuration/runtime dependencies: none. Prisma client regeneration and backend/frontend deployment required. Security: roles/sections, exact source versions, transactions, immutable posted lists, bounded selections (500), idempotency and foreign keys; Applicant APIs expose only the requesting applicant's checklist, never other passers. Privacy: no new external services; snapshots contain staff-authorized applicant names/scores, not document data. Accessibility: labeled controls, status/error text, keyboard-accessible list disclosures and responsive read-only checklist. Legacy payment functions remain retired; no fund release, claiming, reconciliation or monetary audit workflow was added.

### Validation and limitations

Initial regression failures were reviewed individually before fixture updates: required counts changed with optional Indigency; subsequent-routing fixtures needed an explicit original period; acceptance fixtures now need a posted member and approved initial files. Existing denial, stale-result, transaction and duplicate assertions were retained, with added negative cases. Automatic review rejected two combined edits; the user explicitly approved the concrete correction list before those edits proceeded.

Final validation: backend suite passed 315 tests with one existing opt-in database test skipped (316 total); frontend suite passed all 17 modules, including optional capture readiness. Frontend lint/production build and Prisma generate/validate passed. The existing large-chunk build advisory remains. Embedded PostgreSQL migration checks and both isolated browser workflows passed; whitespace checks passed. No hosted acceptance was performed. New tests cover draft retention, atomic posting/rollback, idempotent requests, stale/failed/wrong-exam selections, revision preservation, no-verified-docs acceptance denial, Private receipt enforcement, pre-Scholar Admin uploads, route permissions, optional Indigency, initial and late Private Payroll and proof-only approval. An isolated browser verified draft→post→Admin capture of four Public files with no Indigency→acceptance, and a mobile Applicant checklist without initial-upload controls. Embedded PostgreSQL applied the migration and verified posted header/member immutability, restricted source deletion, matching periods and reasoned retained revisions. This engine is temporary QA tooling, not an application dependency. No production accounts/documents were used and no production acceptance was performed.

Known limitations: visible Applicant/Scholar updates poll every two minutes or load immediately on reload. List index returns up to 100 current-period lists. Hosted authenticated acceptance remains for staff. Legacy JSON without original-period metadata is interpreted in the primary period; it is not rewritten. Review imported records with ambiguous original periods before first processing. A posted list is never edited in place; use a revision and retain the original. Migration supports PostgreSQL; provider migration success must be confirmed because public health does not expose the revision.

### Rollback and next work

Revert application code as a coordinated frontend/backend rollback if necessary. Retain the new tables, immutable snapshots and existing documents; do not drop posted records. Prior code can ignore additive tables, but restoring old code restores pre-verification acceptance, so assess new pending passers first. Use the staff checklist for hosted Public/Private, failed-result publication, phone intake, late and subsequent-period verification. Hostinger frontend verified live: `/assets/index-CwEOhbP7.js`, Admin `Dashboard-CfMC3KSs.js`, Applicant `ApplicantDashboard-DYAZoEOm.js` and Scholar `ScholarDashboard-D5teRJoe.js`. Served assets contain the Passer Lists/post/verification/revision controls, applicant initial checklist, optional labels and processingRoute support. Public API health was healthy/database connected. The user confirmed successful Hostinger backend deployment for `85d78d4`, including migration `20261016010000_passer_lists`, on 2026-10-16. A follow-up public check returned healthy/database connected. Provider revision/migration success is user-confirmed; public health does not independently identify either. No authenticated hosted acceptance was performed. The final bulk follow-up passed all five targeted list tests and frontend lint/build.

## 2026-10-15 - Remove Decision Reason from Results Acceptance

**TL;DR**
- Removed the Decision reason textarea from the Results applicant drawer and the associated acceptance-button restriction.
- Admin acceptance no longer requires a free-text reason when the eligibility recommendation differs; the server and recommendation compatibility flag now match the UI.
- Published passing result, exact record/version checks, authorized staff decision, eligibility snapshot and operational logging remain; previous reasons are preserved and no migration is needed.
- All 39 selected eligibility/examination integration tests, frontend lint/build and whitespace checks passed. Deployment status is recorded below.

### Objective, previous/new behavior and affected roles

Remove the redundant Decision reason field requested by the user. Previously Admins could enter a reason, and applicants whose recommendation required review or did not meet configured criteria could not be accepted without one. Now Admins can explicitly accept an applicant with a published passing result without typing a reason. Eligibility recommendations remain advisory, with the recommendation and staff identity/time recorded. Failed or unpublished results and stale/mismatched records still cannot be accepted. This is a material acceptance-policy change accompanying the field removal, not merely hiding the textarea.

### Implementation and data flow

`frontend/src/ResultsManagement.jsx` no longer renders the field, stores its state, sends reviewReason, or disables acceptance on its absence. Removed obsolete `.rm-decision-reason` styles from `frontend/src/styles/admin.css`. `backend/controllers/applicationController.js` no longer rejects missing reasons. It still accepts optional bounded reasons from older clients and stores null when omitted, preserving earlier records. Operational event classification uses the actual recommendation rather than the old reason-required flag, and its description records a staff decision without claiming a written explanation. `backend/services/eligibilityRecommendation.js` retains `requiresOverrideReason` for compatibility but returns false. No recommendation score, threshold or publication/authorization checks changed.

### Impacts

API: acceptance permits omitted reasons; recommendation response flag reflects optional reasons. Database: no schema changes or record deletion; new decisions may have null review_reason. Configuration/dependencies: no changes. Security: the mandatory text gate is removed, while existing authentication, authorization, record binding, concurrency and passing/publication guards remain. ## 2026-10-14 - Photo-Specific Document Capture Tips

**TL;DR**
- Admins see tips beneath captured-photo previews on the phone and in the initial-requirements intake; advice follows the selected photo, retake, applied crop and rotation.
- Basic pixel checks suggest improvements for dim lighting, uneven lighting, low contrast, little visible detail, soft detail and small images. Up to three tips appear per photo.
- Analysis runs locally in the browser with no new API, external image service, persistence or dependency. Tips never block upload or approve documents.
- Five new metric test cases, the full frontend test suite (17 test modules), lint/build and isolated phone/desktop browser workflows passed. Deployment verification is recorded below.

### Objective, previous and new behavior

Help staff improve document photos using advice based on the captured image rather than a fixed checklist. Previously previews provided capture/crop controls without photo-specific guidance. They now show a compact tips card that checks the current preview and offers concrete retake advice, or reports that basic checks found no obvious warning. Staff must still inspect small text and all page edges before confirming the initial set. These checks are advisory and do not determine document validity or approval.

### Affected roles, implementation and data flow

Provincial and Regular Admins with initial-requirements access are affected. `CapturePhotoTips.jsx` analyzes the existing image data URI asynchronously, drops obsolete results when the source changes or the preview unmounts, and gives a manual-inspection fallback if analysis fails. `capturePhotoQuality.js` samples a canvas at a maximum 384-pixel long side, computes luminance percentiles, a 3×3 lighting grid, edge density and Laplacian variance, and considers the original preview dimensions. Application-specific heuristic thresholds produce up to three tips. White low-detail images are not automatically described as glare. The selected preview in `InitialRequirementCapture.jsx` and the pending phone photo in `PhoneCapturePage.jsx` share this component. Existing pairing, PDF assembly and manual confirmation remain intact.

Canvas pixel access uses the standard [Canvas getImageData API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/getImageData); the [OpenCV Laplacian reference](https://docs.opencv.org/4.5.1/d4/d86/group__imgproc__filter.html) explains the underlying derivative operator. These sources do not validate the application's quality thresholds.

### Files and system impacts

Added `frontend/src/CapturePhotoTips.jsx`, `frontend/src/utils/capturePhotoQuality.js` and `frontend/tests/capturePhotoQuality.test.js`; updated both intake components and `frontend/src/styles/document-capture.css`. Added `docs/qa/2026-10-14/photo-tips-acceptance-checklist.md`.

API, database, configuration and dependencies: no changes. Security/authorization: no changes. Privacy: image analysis stays on the device; this feature introduces no image transfer, analytics, stored quality score or third-party service. Existing authorized phone transfer and final upload retain their established behavior. Accessibility: a polite status announcement, text explanations, and a non-color indication of each warning; layout was checked at 390-pixel phone and 1280-pixel desktop widths. Payroll-list scope and legacy payment code: no changes. Deployment: frontend only, no migration. Release `8c0d7dd` was pushed and verified live on Hostinger: `/assets/index-DyohW61F.js`, phone `PhoneCapturePage-kpfgqiaD.js`, Admin `Dashboard-DKK0TpJp.js`, shared tips `document-capture-B57_lj6d.js` and `document-capture-Ckl801Er.css`. Both routes reference the shared advice module; served code includes the dim/size/soft-detail tips, manual-inspection note and analysis fallback. API health remained healthy with database connected. Public verification checked served assets, not an authenticated production capture/upload.

### Validation and results

Five deterministic metric test cases passed, covering sharp, small, dark, blank/low-detail, low-contrast, soft-detail and unevenly lit samples plus invalid sample rejection. The full frontend suite passed all 17 test modules. Frontend lint and production build passed; the existing large-chunk build advisory remains. Isolated Chromium fixtures using synthetic photos and mocked pairing responses passed at phone/desktop widths: dim/detail warnings appeared, retake cleared prior advice, clear samples cleared warnings, small photos and applied crop produced size advice, phone Upload remained enabled and the card stayed within the viewport. Network inspection found only the existing pairing requests, with no analysis endpoint. A stale Vite optimized-dependency response initially prevented fixture rendering; restarting the local QA server resolved it. Temporary fixtures were removed. No real Scholar records or production documents were used during these checks.

### Limitations, rollback and next work

Heuristics can produce false positives/negatives and are evaluated on the processed preview, not the camera's original raw file. They cannot read text, verify readability, identify missing page edges, reliably detect glare/perspective, or validate document content. PDF-only selections have no image preview tips. Physical camera behavior and hosted authenticated uploads still need staff acceptance testing using the checklist. Calibrate advice with representative non-sensitive document captures before treating it as stronger quality screening. Revert the frontend feature files/imports/styles to roll back; no data rollback is required. Tips should remain advisory.
