## 2026-10-14 - Authenticated Phone-to-Laptop Capture Pairing

**TL;DR**
- Admin can pair a phone from the laptop intake using a locally generated QR code; the phone signs in with the same Admin account and sends photos into the correct Scholar/period draft.
- Phone transfer never approves requirements. Laptop confirmation is disabled until the phone connection ends; reviewed documents then use the existing approval/upload flow.
- Removed the separate document-row Upload/Replace buttons and their duplicate handler; viewing/status stay available and corrections use the intake's capture/file controls.
- Added one bounded temporary transfer table, owner/role checks, 20-minute expiry, receipt/cancel cleanup, CAS/retry protection and expiry cleanup. One database migration is required.
- Backend/frontend regression suites, lint/build and two isolated browser workflows passed. Public artifact verification and provider migration confirmation are recorded below.

### Objective and previous/new behavior

Allow staff to keep the Scholar drawer on a laptop while using a phone's rear camera, avoiding a second independent upload workflow. Previously capture could only occur in the current browser/device, and individual document rows duplicated Upload/Replace controls. Now Use phone camera creates a session bound to the initiating Admin, Scholar and academic period; QR points to `/phone-capture?session=...`. Sign-in stays on that route and preserves the session query. The phone can switch Admin accounts without retaining the previous preview/context; the route remounts intake when the authenticated account changes. The QR contains no login token or document data and alone grants no access.

### Roles, implementation and data flow

Existing initial-upload roles apply: Provincial/Regular Admin with Scholars access. The phone and laptop must use the same Admin account. Backend requests authenticate each time, match session owner and recheck active Scholar/period before accessing a queue. Public initial scope has five keys; Private has six. QR rendering uses the local qrcode package, not an external QR service ([upstream browser API](https://github.com/soldair/node-qrcode)).

A UUID session and private context/queued JPEGs are stored in `phone_capture_sessions`, with a fixed 20-minute expiry and revision. Phone frames/photos are normalized locally, previewed, assigned a category and sent with a UUID page ID. Sending only queues a temporary photo: it does not mutate initial documents, review decisions, continuing submissions or list membership. Each photo must be a JPEG with a signature and below 4 MB; queue total is bounded at 32 MB encoded, ten pending pages per category, and three live sessions per Admin. Creating a new pairing for the same owner/Scholar/period replaces the old pairing and its undelivered queue; other Scholar sessions are untouched.

The laptop polls every three seconds while visible/not processing. It imports pages into the existing intake, enforcing applicable categories, page and draft-size limits; existing PDF drafts or already-uploaded categories hold incoming pages for staff resolution. UUID receipt tracking prevents replay from duplicating drafts. Draft updates use a synchronous local reference so transfer does not overwrite local edits. The server acknowledgement deletes only imported temporary pages. Concurrent send/ack uses revision compare-and-swap with bounded retries so pending pages are not overwritten. After receipt, editing/cropping/ordering remains on the laptop. Ending a connection first calls the authenticated freeze endpoint: CAS sets its JSON context to stop new sends and returns the last queued photos. The laptop receives these before deleting the session; if a category is blocked/full, it keeps the frozen queue for resolution instead of discarding photos. The phone stops capture when it observes this frozen state. Normal close requires a frozen session and a matching revision; older clients cannot silently close an active transfer queue. Intake cancellation explicitly requests discard and warns while a phone is paired. During mixed frontend/backend rollout, a missing freeze endpoint with an existing session blocks close/approval until the backend update is ready. Staff must end the phone connection, review the complete set and check the approval confirmation before the original initial upload endpoint is called. Partial final-upload retry remains unchanged.

The phone polls metadata every ten seconds; server-supplied remaining time drives expiry, avoiding reliance on the phone clock. Cancellation/deletion prevents future access; phone notices closure/expiry on its next poll and stops camera tracks. Camera cleanup/permission behavior remains as in direct intake. Laptop unmount attempts authenticated session deletion; fixed expiry is the fallback when a browser cannot send cleanup. API janitor removes expired queues every minute while running, and create/expired access also purges expired rows. Temporary drafts received on the laptop remain in tab memory and are lost on leaving intake/reload as previously explained.

### Changed areas and impacts

- Backend: phoneCaptureController, guarded application routes, operational activity mappings for pairing creation/closure, periodic server cleanup, phone session regression tests.
- Database: additive `phone_capture_sessions` UUID/context/pages/revision/expiry table, indexes and Scholar/period foreign keys. Migration `20261014020000_phone_capture_sessions`; application/legacy/cleaned schema definitions synchronized. No existing record/file migration or deletion.
- API: authenticated POST `/phone-capture/sessions`, GET/DELETE `/phone-capture/sessions/:id`, POST `/pages`, `/received` and `/freeze`. Responses are private/no-store; wrong-owner IDs return 404; expired sessions return 410. Mutations have a dedicated 180-per-15-minute rate limit in addition to existing API/auth limits.
- Frontend: LaptopPhoneCapture, PhoneCapturePage, InitialRequirementCapture draft/pairing integration, ScholarsManagement row simplification, App route, capture styles and static route fallback generation.
- Configuration/dependencies: qrcode 1.5.4 added to frontend lock/package files; no new environment variable. Existing API base and Admin authentication remain. Production build generates `/phone-capture` static fallback.
- Security/privacy: UUIDs are identifiers, not bearer authorization. No account/token sharing via QR; photos are temporarily stored in the same managed database and accessible only to the initiating authenticated Admin with Scholars access. Receipt/cancel/expiry removes active queue rows/images. Existing database backup-retention policy is unchanged. QR/context is not recorded in activity descriptions. No public document link or third-party image processing; no microphone, mail or notification feature added.
- Accessibility: named QR image and alternative link, native capture input/selects, login on the pairing route, account switching, status messages, responsive controls and explicit disabled approval while paired. Physical QR scanning/camera quality remain a device trial.
- Deployment: frontend/backend release; apply the new migration before pairing tests. Existing permanent document storage/version policy remains authoritative. Legacy monetary operations remain retired; no payment-release, disbursement or monetary-audit workflow added.

### Validation and results

Full regression suites passed: 297 backend + 74 frontend = 371 checks, with one optional real-database test skipped. Coverage includes session owner isolation, Public/Private category scope, idempotent send, metadata/image separation, selective receipt cleanup, CAS retry, limits, expiry/cancel/purge, same-record pairing replacement and actual HTTP role/section authentication. Frontend lint/build and diff whitespace checks passed; existing large-chunk advisory remains. Two isolated browser workflows (Public laptop 1280px/phone 390px; Private laptop 1024px/phone 390px) passed QR generation/alternative URL, login preserving the pairing URL, photo transfer into per-category laptop drafts, duplicate delivery/ack cleanup, confirmation disabled while paired, final PDF upload after closure, a photo queued immediately before closure retained in the generated PDF, phone closure notice and removal of row upload controls. No real hosted photos or official lists were mutated. Real PostgreSQL migration/locking and physical QR/camera quality were not exercised locally.

### Limitations, rollback and next work

Polling gives near-real-time transfer, not live video streaming. Browser tabs must remain open; drafts are not durable after receipt. A failed acknowledgement can retry safely within the same laptop session. Undelivered pages expire; restarting the same pairing intentionally discards that old queue. If a category already has a PDF or ten pages, resolve it on the laptop before continuing. The phone sends photos only; the laptop's Choose file remains the PDF fallback. Receiving the full set does not authenticate the paper's content: staff still check legibility, completeness and identity. The expiry janitor depends on the API being running; expired access is still denied and stale rows purge after service resumes. Database backups may retain historical row versions under existing policy.

Before rollback, close/purge temporary sessions and preserve permanent documents. Keep the additive table during a code rollback and clean any stale queues; older code cannot run the new cleanup job. Roll back frontend/backend together; no permanent Scholar data rollback required. Follow `docs/qa/2026-10-14/phone-pairing-acceptance-checklist.md`, confirm Hostinger migration success and test physical phone/laptop connectivity.

Deployment: initial code release `9a99e7d` pushed to main. The frontend entry `/assets/index-CwPcr0yK.js`, Admin `Dashboard-D8xI7v8u.js` and phone `PhoneCapturePage-CG2wHkP-.js` were verified live, including the static phone route and absence of row upload markup. User confirmed the requested backend/migration deployment. Public API health is healthy/database connected; unauthenticated phone API requests return 401 at the existing shared-access gate, which does not verify route revision. Final code release `b25d398` was pushed and verified live: entry `/assets/index-Bzpec87e.js`, Admin `Dashboard-CbcIMVml.js` and phone `PhoneCapturePage-CZMWZbV-.js` contain the freeze/final-photo receiving sequence; the phone static fallback matches the live entry and row upload markup remains absent. User confirmed successful backend deployment for `b25d398`; no additional migration was needed. API/database health remains good. Authenticated hosted transfers and physical camera/QR quality remain staff acceptance tests.

## 2026-10-14 - Camera-First Initial Requirements Intake

**TL;DR**
- Authorized Admins can capture the complete initial set directly in the Scholar drawer, replacing printer scanning and manual file lookup with guided camera intake.
- Public five/Private six requirements have separate previews and records; staff explicitly confirm readability, completeness, replacement and approval before uploading.
- Multipage PDFs, margin cropping, rotation, retake, page ordering and scanned-file fallback are supported; successful uploads are retained when a later upload fails.
- No backend, database migration or dependency changes. Drafts stay in memory and camera tracks stop on exit/backgrounding.
- Frontend tests, lint/build and synthetic desktop/mobile camera checks passed. Physical-device capture quality and hosted authenticated uploads require the acceptance trial below.

### Objective and previous/new behavior

Replace the receive-hard-copy → printer scan → locate/upload each file routine with receive-hard-copy → open the correct Scholar → capture each requirement → review/confirm the initial set. The drawer's Capture initial requirements action guides staff through applicable document categories. Live camera prefers an outward-facing camera, while Take photo uses the phone camera chooser where supported. Staff can also select an existing JPG/PNG/PDF. Existing individual Upload/Replace controls remain as the correction/fallback route.

### Roles, implementation and data flow

Only staff already permitted to upload initial requirements see the intake action; unknown school classification disables capture. Scholar identity and academic period remain visible in intake; the component is keyed by applicant/period so drafts cannot carry to another record. Public initial documents exclude tuition receipt; Private initial documents include it. Existing approved initial files can be retained, while a missing/pending/rejected requirement needs a capture or file. Each new capture/file resets confirmation.

Live frames and selected photos are normalized through canvas into JPEG pixels up to 2200px on the longest side. Staff review page previews, trim each margin with labeled sliders, rotate, remove/retake and reorder pages. Up to ten pages per requirement become one A4 PDF; the generated data URL is normalized to the existing backend contract. All pending documents are prepared and checked against the 6 MB per-document limit before any upload begins. Photo draft memory is bounded; PDF fallback uses the same existing 6 MB limit. No draft is written to localStorage, IndexedDB, a server or an external processing service before confirmation.

Staff must check the final confirmation that every requirement (including retained originals) is readable, complete and ready for approval, and that captures replace existing files for the selected period. Requests then use the existing Admin initial-upload endpoint sequentially with the selected applicant and period. The backend's existing staff-upload autoapproval/version retention remains unchanged. Each successful response clears only that draft and locks that successful category within the current intake. A failure keeps remaining drafts for retry and refreshes the Scholar record; confirmed successes are skipped. There is no atomic bulk upload transaction. Network ambiguity after a server commit can create another retained version on retry, so verify the drawer before repeating an interrupted upload.

Camera permission is requested only on an explicit live-camera action, with no microphone request. Tracks stop on changing requirements, leaving the intake/drawer, changing browser visibility or navigating away. Late camera resolutions are stopped after cancellation/unmount. Closing intake prompts before discarding drafts; a page reload/close receives a browser draft warning. Leaving Overview or closing the drawer discards drafts, as explained in the intake. Pending HTTP work is aborted on unmount, but a server request already committed cannot be undone.

### Changed areas and impacts

- Frontend: new InitialRequirementCapture component, documentCapture canvas/PDF utility, scoped capture styles, Scholar drawer integration and readiness regression checks.
- API: no new endpoint or changed contract. Existing authenticated `/scholars/:applicantId/requirements/:requirementKey` remains authoritative for role, active Scholar, selected period and Private receipt guards.
- Database/configuration: no migration, new environment setting, dependency or storage change. Original/continuing document sets, replacement archives and operational upload logs remain intact.
- Security/privacy: camera/photo/PDF work is local until confirmation; no cross-account session transfer or public capture link. Existing private storage and ownership controls apply after upload. No emails or notifications are sent by this intake. Physical camera permission/device support depends on the browser.
- Accessibility: labeled controls, native photo/file inputs and trim sliders, keyboard focus, named previews, pressed states for category/page selection, busy/status messages, disabled unavailable controls. Controls wrap inside the responsive drawer.
- Deployment: frontend-only main-branch release for Hostinger; no new backend revision/migration required for camera intake. Existing schedule migration confirmation remains separate.
- Product scope: no change to list eligibility or legacy payment code; workflow still ends with official payroll-list generation.

### Validation and results

Frontend regression suite passed, including new incomplete/approved-retained/successful-retry readiness checks. Frontend lint and production build passed; the existing large-chunk advisory remains. Diff whitespace checks passed. Synthetic Chromium runs for Public at 1280px and Private at 390px passed fake live camera capture, native-photo input, crop/rotation, retake, multipage PDF page count and exact upload data URL contract, role-visible initial intake, selected applicant/period scope, mandatory confirmation, simulated third-file failure, successful-file skipping on retry, permission denial fallback and camera-track cleanup on drawer close. The mobile screenshot was reviewed for fit and readability. No real hosted documents, official lists or production uploads were mutated during verification.

### Limitations, rollback and recommended next work

This is guided capture, not OCR, automatic edge detection, perspective correction or proof of authenticity. Cropping is manual and staff must assess lighting, focus, missing pages and legibility. Phone camera/file-picker behavior and PDF preview vary by browser/OS; live camera needs a secure context and permission ([MDN camera reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia), [MDN capture attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/capture)). Use an authorized phone login rather than sharing a desktop session. Drafts are intentionally temporary and not recoverable after leaving the intake/drawer. Maintain original hard copies under existing CAO policy; this feature does not authorize their disposal.

Rollback the frontend integration/component/styles/utilities to remove intake; existing uploaded documents remain readable through the established preview/replacement flow, with no database rollback. Confirm readability and capture time on the actual CAO phone/webcam before replacing the printer routine operationally. Use `docs/qa/2026-10-14/camera-intake-acceptance-checklist.md` for testing.

Deployment: frontend code release `0a995dd` pushed to main and verified live on Hostinger. Entry `/assets/index-Cm1PnmYY.js`, Admin `Dashboard-BknymIeQ.js` and stylesheet `Dashboard-Bqe0vOoN.css` expose camera intake, native phone capture, crop/retake/page ordering and explicit upload/approve actions. The generated-PDF MIME contract is present; `jspdf.es.min-CUBsX9lU.js` is served with HTTP 200. No new migration or backend change. Public artifact checks do not claim authenticated hosted document uploads or real-camera image quality.

## 2026-10-14 - Continuing Requirement Schedules and Late-Submission Windows

**TL;DR**
- Admin can publish one continuing schedule per school year/semester, plus a separate late window for all or selected active scholars.
- Scheduled uploads automatically become available after all five Public or six Private initial documents are approved; no individual opening click is required.
- Public processing sessions open Payroll. Incomplete requirements remain warnings; existing list membership prevents duplicate inclusion in the same period.
- Original/continuing documents and their histories remain separate. One additive schedule-table migration is required; no document or legacy monetary records are deleted.
- Verification: 360 automated checks passed, one optional database migration check skipped; lint/build and synthetic desktop/mobile browser scenarios passed. Hostinger deployment status is recorded below.

### Objective and previous/new behavior

Remove repeated individual opening clicks and provide a controlled way to accept late continuing documents in their original academic semester. Previously CAO opened each scholar manually; the academic-period deadline blocked late Scholar uploads and the preparation drawer always opened Billing. The new Scholars → Continuing Requirements tab publishes regular opening/closing timestamps, optional late timestamps, and all/selected Scholar scope. The original regular deadline remains stored separately from the late deadline. Without a published schedule, legacy manual opening/deadline behavior remains compatible, but the manual UI button is replaced by schedule guidance.

### Roles, workflow, implementation and data flow

Provincial/Regular Admins with Scholars access publish schedules; authorized Billing staff with Scholars access can view them. Initial ownership remains CAO for every initial file (Public five, Private six including tuition receipt). Scholars own continuing grades/registration and Private-only tuition receipts. The service checks persisted initial approvals and the server clock; unknown classification fails closed. Scheduled dates, selected late IDs and an optimistic revision are stored per academic period. Stale saves return 409, invalid/inactive periods and unavailable selected Scholars are rejected. Time inputs use the browser's labeled local timezone and transmit timezone-qualified ISO values.

Regular access requires approved initial files and an inclusive opening/deadline interval. Late access additionally requires the all/selected authorization; the late window must begin after the regular deadline. Initial approval is evaluated on each read/upload: approval after the opening time opens access automatically while a permitted window remains active. Later revoked initial approval closes scheduled upload access without deleting files. Read projections expose the continuing wave after opening; actual uploads recheck the period/window and approval within the existing document transaction. Existing version/history and private storage behavior are retained. No per-Scholar timer job or bulk mutation is needed.

Scholars can select another still-active submission period in the requirements panel, including an earlier semester's late window; the primary dashboard's exam/payroll context remains unchanged. Admin period summaries and generation/reporting warnings use the scheduled wave rather than treating initial grades as continuing completion. Portal refresh remains two minutes and Admin directory refresh five minutes; reload is appropriate for immediate testing.

Payroll generation is independent of submission deadlines and document completeness. Additional lists for previously unlisted Public scholars in the same semester use the existing generator. Already-listed scholars can complete documents during an authorized window without another payroll entry. The drawer resolves Public→Payroll and Private→Billing and verifies destination section access. Existing hard account/classification/route/duplicate guards remain. Existing legacy billing metadata storage is retained for preparation compatibility; legacy disbursement/payment endpoints remain retired. No fund-release or monetary-audit workflow is introduced.

### Changed system areas and impacts

- Backend: continuing schedule controller/service, application routes/controller, lifecycle report controller, operational activity mapping, and schedule/ownership/payroll regression fixtures.
- Frontend: ContinuingRequirementsSettings, ScholarsManagement, ScholarDashboard and their schedule/period-selector styles.
- API: authenticated GET/PUT `/scholars/continuing-schedules/:id`; optional `requirementPeriodId` on the owner's application response; schedule/access metadata in Scholar responses. Upload/list endpoint contracts remain compatible.
- Database: additive `continuing_requirement_schedules` table, primary period key, timestamp/range/scope constraints, selected applicant IDs, revision and updating actor. Migration `20261014010000_continuing_requirement_schedules`; application, legacy and cleaned schema definitions updated. No file/history migration or destructive data change.
- Configuration: no new environment variables or dependencies. Published continuing schedules govern continuing uploads; older Settings deadlines remain the fallback for periods without one. No production schedule is seeded automatically.
- Security/privacy: role and Scholars-section checks, owner-only uploads, active-scholar validation, stale-save protection, server-side date/scope enforcement. Selected IDs appear only in authorized Admin configuration responses; Scholar status reveals only their own late authorization. Existing private document storage is unchanged. No mail/notification sends added.
- Accessibility: labeled controls, keyboard native inputs/checkboxes, status/error regions, disabled unavailable actions, and responsive single-column date fields. Section buttons use pressed state.
- Deployment: push main for separate Hostinger frontend/backend builds; backend must apply the new migration before schedule testing. Provider revision/migration confirmation is required because public health exposes no release ID.

### Validation and results

Full suites passed: 288 backend + 72 frontend = 360 checks; one optional real-database catalog migration check skipped. New checks cover Public/Private initial completeness, exact time boundaries, late all/selected authorization, preserved original deadlines, legacy compatibility, scope projection, stale/invalid schedule saves, inactive periods, real Express role guards, real upload controllers without manual opening, selected-period portal behavior and list-warning independence. Frontend lint/build, backend syntax checks and diff whitespace checks passed; the existing large-chunk build advisory remains.

Synthetic Chromium scenarios at 1280px and 390px verify date publishing/timezone conversion, selected late scope, saved-schedule reload, absence of the individual opening button, Public Payroll navigation, Scholar late upload scope, closed-window blocking and pending-initial blocking. Browser APIs use synthetic fixtures; no hosted Scholar documents, real list generation or live scheduling were mutated. Real PostgreSQL migration execution/concurrency and production blob-upload behavior were not exercised locally.

### Limitations, rollback and recommended next work

A late window is one configurable interval per period; additional windows replace its configuration, preserving the original regular deadline but not a separate full schedule-version archive. Operational mutation logs remain available. Selected scopes are capped at 500; inactive academic periods cannot accept uploads. Activate an earlier genuine semester to accept its late files rather than creating a fictitious period. Legacy initial documents continue using the existing first-period association rules. Unknown school classification or missing initial approvals requires correction before scheduled uploads; list generation still permits incomplete documents.

Keep the additive table on rollback and pause writes before restoring an older release. Back up schedules/documents first; older code cannot enforce the new late-window rules and can use older per-period deadlines/manual flags. Prefer a forward correction. Existing document-wave rollback precautions still apply. Follow the linked acceptance checklist and confirm Hostinger migration success before hosted authenticated testing.

Deployment: code release `96d24e4` pushed to GitHub main. Public Hostinger entry `/assets/index-C8PkNo2x.js`, Admin `Dashboard-gbJkXqz3.js`, and Scholar `ScholarDashboard-BWqGIzEW.js` verified live with schedule controls, Public Payroll action, submission-period selector and late/waiting messages. API health is healthy/database connected; the new schedule route returns 401 without authentication. This verifies route presence and access protection, not the deployed backend commit or table migration. Hostinger backend/migration confirmation remains pending; no hosted authenticated scheduling/uploads/list generation was performed.

Acceptance checklist: `docs/qa/2026-10-14/continuing-schedules-acceptance-checklist.md`.

## 2026-10-14 - Separate Admin Initial and Scholar Continuing Requirements

**TL;DR**
- CAO uploads the complete initial set: tax exemption, indigency, ID, grades, registration form, and tuition receipt for Private-school scholars only.
- Scholars upload only continuing grades/registration/Private tuition receipts after authorized staff opens the second wave for that scholar and academic period; initial records remain separate and visible.
- Period/wave records, file versions, and review history are preserved; JSON compare-and-swap retries prevent simultaneous uploads from losing other files, and stale single/bulk reviews are rejected.
- Verification: 337 tests passed, one opt-in real-database test skipped; lint/build and four synthetic Public/Private desktop/mobile browser scenarios passed. Release 32b0c35 pushed; frontend verified live and API/database health passed. Backend revision confirmation pending; no schema migration.

### Objective and previous/new behavior

Implement the user-approved distinction between submission waves rather than fixed document types. Previously admins could upload only three initial documents, Scholars owned grades/registration/tuition from the outset, and all uploads shared one application requirement map. Files could overwrite prior waves, and parallel writes could lose another document. Now admins can upload five Public/six Private initial requirements. Admin intake continues to approve checked documents immediately, as in the existing workflow. Scholars see a read-only initial checklist and can upload two Public/three Private continuing documents only when CAO opens their continuing submission. CAO may open the second wave in the same academic period or a later one; initial completion is not a new gate on opening the wave or generating lists.

The original initial set is retained with its academic-period identity and referenced by later continuing periods. A deliberately recorded initial update in a later period is stored separately and overrides that period's initial projection. Continuing grades/registration/receipts come only from that period's continuing set, never from the old initial approvals. Previously recorded legacy files retain their uploader/review metadata and are identified as previously recorded rather than attributed to a new admin upload.

### Roles, implementation, and data flow

Provincial Admin and Administrator accounts with Scholars access upload initial files and open continuing submissions. Billing / Payroll Admin and Provincial Admin review permissions remain unchanged. Scholar uploads require an active accepted account and its own application, a real explicitly selected active period, an opened continuing wave, and the existing continuing submission deadline. Private receipt routing is validated against the saved school; Public receipt attempts are rejected. Initial staff intake remains available independently of the Scholar deadline.

The existing application initial_docs JSON now holds requirementSets keyed by academic period/wave, initialRequirementPeriodId, and requirementWaves opening metadata. Each stored file has its upload actor/role/time, version identifier, revision, and review metadata. Replacing a file archives its prior version and review history without deleting its private blob. Legacy originals remain in their original root map and are adopted into the primary-period initial set on the first scoped mutation; deterministic version IDs make legacy previews/reviews addressable. No original upload dates or reviewers are invented. Only unsuccessful new blob uploads are cleaned up.

All affected document writes use a transaction and compare the complete previously read JSON snapshot before saving. Conflicting uploads retry against fresh data. Reviews require the exact period, wave, file version, and review revision; bulk approvals also require the pending-file snapshot. Priority-proof review merges only its own proof and retains existing wave records and acceptance behavior. File previews select their exact set/version, including previous versions, through existing authenticated document streaming.

Scholar Management exposes separate initial/continuing checklists, an Open continuing submission action, and previous file versions. Scholar Dashboard exposes the initial set as read-only and enables only continuing uploads in the second wave. Document Reviews groups each period/wave separately, displays human-readable period labels, and shows prior review decisions. Billing/Payroll warning snapshots, applicant guidance, and lifecycle reports use the applicable wave projection; legacy approval columns cannot clear an empty continuing set. List generation still permits incomplete requirements with warnings, retains fixed grant amounts, and enforces account/classification/route/duplicate gates.

### Files and system areas

- New backend requirementWaves service: scoped records, original-set references, versions/history, and guarded transactional mutations.
- Application/document-review controllers and application routes: initial/continuing uploads, wave opening, projections, previews, scoped reviews/bulk approval, and priority-proof compatibility.
- Document-review/applicant-guidance services and lifecycle reporting: wave-aware records, guidance, and requirement completeness.
- Scholar Management, Scholar Dashboard, Document Reviews, new frontend scope utility, and scholar portal styles: ownership/checklists, scoped requests, period labels, and history.
- New backend/frontend wave regressions, updated document ownership/payroll fixtures, root summary, detailed log, and the dated testing checklist.

### API, database, configuration, security, privacy, accessibility, and deployment impact

API: existing upload endpoints remain, with explicit academicPeriodId required. Admin uploads always target initial; Scholar uploads always target continuing. Added PUT /scholars/:applicantId/continuing-requirements/open guarded by existing authentication, admin role, and Scholars-section access. Application/management responses add wave/checklist/history metadata. Preview/review requests include academic period and wave; file versions and revisions protect stale decisions. Unscoped priority-proof requests retain their existing purpose. Older cached normal review/upload clients must refresh rather than guessing a set.

Database: no schema migration or new relational table. Scoped document records live in the existing JSON column; legacy scalar requirement rows and list/history storage remain intact. No destructive backfill, historical rewrite, or file deletion. Configuration/dependencies: no new settings, environment variables, or libraries; existing private document blob storage is used. Security: role/section/ownership guards are preserved, no client-supplied file approval is trusted, and concurrency/stale-review controls are strengthened. Privacy: historical files remain private; review queues expose metadata rather than blob URLs/file data, and all verification uses synthetic records. Accessibility: existing file controls/keyboard review dialogs remain; initial ownership and continuing-open/closed states are explicit. Deployment: frontend/backend must be released together; no migration required.

### Scope boundary

This change handles scholar document intake/review and list-preparation warnings. It adds no fund release, claiming, disbursement, reconciliation, or monetary auditing. Legacy payroll/claim storage remains retained for existing list/history compatibility, with retired payment operations still disabled. Activity Logs continue to record operational record changes only.

### Validation and results

Full regression results: 265 backend and 72 frontend tests passed; one opt-in real-database catalog migration test skipped. Wave tests exercise full initial ownership, Private/Public receipts, closed/open continuing access, same-period and next-period separation, initial reuse without copying old academic approvals, parallel admin/admin and admin/Scholar writes, preserved file/review history, exact-version previews, stale single/bulk reviews, deadline behavior, inactive/invalid periods, actual authenticated route guards, and priority-proof compatibility. A Payroll controller regression confirms continuing completeness does not inherit initial approval columns while incomplete records can still be listed. Frontend scope regressions confirm exact set/version requests and unchanged unscoped priority-proof requests.

Frontend lint, production build, JavaScript syntax checks, and diff whitespace validation passed. The build retains its existing large-chunk advisory. Four Chromium scenarios (Public/Private at 1280px/390px) passed with intercepted APIs: all admin initial uploads, read-only initial Scholar checklist, closed/open continuing controls, scoped Scholar grade upload, unchanged initial files, separate review groups, exact-period/file preview, and scoped approval. No production scholar or document records were modified by verification.

### Limitations, rollback considerations, and recommended next work

Legacy files without reliable period provenance are associated with the configured primary period on first scoped mutation while original root data/metadata are retained. Files deleted by older code cannot be reconstructed; version retention applies going forward. Real PostgreSQL contention and production blob uploads were not executed; tests use facades/intercepted APIs. Read-only initial files reused in later periods have no new expiry policy; staff must replace expired/changed documents according to CAO policy. Historical storage grows because replaced files are retained; any retention/deletion policy requires a separate decision. Scholar portals retain the existing two-minute visible-page refresh, so manually reload during immediate testing. Batch intake across files/scholars is not added by this release.

Prefer a forward correction if issues arise. Before reverting to code that does not understand waves, pause document uploads/reviews and preserve a database/storage backup; old replacement handlers can delete blobs referenced by retained sets. Do not flatten, delete, or overwrite wave records as a rollback shortcut. Use the dated acceptance checklist with synthetic accepted scholars after both deployments succeed. Deployment results will be recorded after public verification and provider confirmation.

Previously the privileged role was labeled Super Admin/Super Administrator in the app shell, sidebar, staff selector/stat/password confirmation, settings guidance, dashboard display, and relevant API messages. The existing examination integration test explicitly verifies both the saved attendance status and timestamp returned by the applicant API. Attendance frontend/controller/helper implementation is unchanged. The dated verification report records the findings.

### API, database, configuration, security, privacy, accessibility, and deployment

API: staff roleLabel/error text changes; wire role remains SuperAdmin and attendance routes/responses are unchanged. Database/schema/migration/data: no impact; database superadmin/is_super_admin fields and existing accounts are retained. Configuration: none. Security: existing role/section guards, full-access defaults, self-protection, and final-active-admin protections are unchanged. Privacy: no new fields or external services; all verification used synthetic fixture records. Accessibility: existing controls remain, with updated visible labels/role initial. Deployment: frontend/backend both need releasing for consistent display/error text; no migration. No deployment performed in this task. ### Validation and results

The full regression suites passed (242 backend plus 70 frontend tests; one opt-in real-database migration test skipped). Frontend lint and production build passed, retaining the existing large-chunk advisory. The targeted real-controller examination integration suite passed after adding status/timestamp read-back assertions for both modes. Chromium tested the actual applicant component with intercepted APIs and a controlled clock: after an attendance save in an isolated browser context, the applicant remained Pending before the next poll and became Present at 120 seconds. A same-context sibling's localStorage revision triggered an immediate refetch. Sidebar browser rendering showed Provincial Admin Workspace while using the unchanged SuperAdmin role. No live credentials or production records were used.

### Limitations, rollback, and recommended next work

Hosted authenticated attendance changes were not executed. Timing tests used intercepted browser APIs and backend database facades; successful network requests and visible-page scheduling are assumed. Network latency and hidden tabs can extend the observed delay. No instant server-push channel exists in this path. Recommend a short examination-specific refresh interval (such as five seconds during the active attendance/start window) if near-immediate cross-device reflection is required; true push would require a separate SSE/WebSocket implementation. Neither is introduced by this verification request. Roll back display strings/service labels to restore the former title; no data rollback is needed. Deploy frontend/backend together when requested, then verify with synthetic applicants/staff.

## 2026-10-13 - Remove Billing and Payroll Requirement Overrides

**TL;DR**
- Active scholars can enter their correctly routed certification/payroll list even when applicable requirements are missing or unapproved; no individual override authorization or reason is needed.
- Staff retain bulk queue controls; incomplete requirements appear as warnings, while account, classification, routing, period, and duplicate checks remain enforced.
- Document approvals, historical list records, and operational Activity Logs are preserved; the workflow still ends at list generation.
- Validation: 312 regression tests passed, one opt-in database test skipped; frontend lint and production build passed. Four local desktop/mobile browser scenarios passed. This change has not been deployed.

### Objective and reason

Remove repeated override clicks while permitting scholars with incomplete requirements to enter official lists, as explicitly requested. The earlier proposal to require all approvals before listing was superseded by this instruction.

### Previous and new behavior

Previously, missing/unapproved requirements blocked normal processing; Super Admin or Billing / Payroll Admin could queue each exception through a reason dialog. Now document readiness is informational for list generation. Authorized processing staff, including Regular Admin with the existing section access, can queue these scholars individually or through the existing Move all control. Incomplete requirements remain marked and are counted in the generation response and success notice. Inactive/unavailable scholars, unknown school classifications, wrong school routes, inactive processing periods, and existing period memberships remain blocked. Pending documents remain pending.

### Roles, implementation, and data flow

The shared list eligibility evaluator separates missing/unapproved-document warnings from hard blockers. Scholar Management returns processingWarnings independently of processing eligibility and existing document status. Billing and Payroll controllers re-evaluate saved records before generating lists, record outstanding-document descriptions in new membership notes, and include incompleteRequirementsCount in their responses and operational log descriptions. The frontend removes override state, labels, dialog, and request fields. Bulk queueing is retained; refresh recalculates queued eligibility. The period selector still clears the queue. Billing details editing keeps its shared modal layout under appropriately named styles.

### Changed areas

- Backend lifecycle integrity service and application controller: list eligibility, retired request handling, list notes, responses, and Activity Logs.
- Frontend BillingPayrollManagement, processingVisibility helper, and admin styles: normal queueing, warnings, retained editor, removed override controls.
- Backend lifecycle/payroll regressions and frontend processing/identity regressions: updated policy expectations and direct-controller safeguards.
- Verification checklist: docs/qa/2026-10-13/billing-payroll-listing-checklist.md.

### API, database, configuration, security, privacy, accessibility, and deployment

API: existing processing routes and access guards remain. Nonempty or malformed billingOverrides/payrollOverrides return HTTP 400 with refresh guidance; empty arrays from older clients remain compatible. overrideCount is replaced with incompleteRequirementsCount. Scholar Management adds processingWarnings. Database: no schema migration or historical data rewrite; new list membership notes preserve outstanding requirements at generation. Missing Private requirement rows can be created with the existing period/reference fields without creating approvals. Configuration: no changes. Security: document-completion gating is deliberately relaxed, while authentication, role/section access, server routing, inactive-account and duplicate guards remain. Privacy: existing authenticated response scope remains; no new personal fields or external services. Accessibility: warnings use visible text, and normal keyboard-operable queue controls remain; no extra confirmation modal is introduced. Deployment: frontend and backend must be released together; no deployment performed in this task.

### Scope and historical data

Legacy payroll_batches/payroll_claims storage and Private batch status values are retained for list/history compatibility. They continue to represent list records in this workflow; fund release, claiming, disbursement, reconciliation, and monetary auditing remain disabled/outside scope. Historical override reasons and Activity Logs are retained. The separate scholarship-acceptance eligibility override is unchanged.

### Validation and results

The full fixture-based regression suites passed: 242 backend plus 70 frontend tests; one real-database catalog migration test intentionally skipped. Tests cover missing/pending documents, processing roles, warning metadata, unchanged approvals, generation without a Private requirement row, retired override requests, and retained hard blockers. Frontend lint, production build, and diff whitespace validation passed. The build retains the existing large-chunk advisory. Four Chromium scenarios passed (Billing and Payroll at 1280px and 390px) using synthetic records and intercepted API requests: absent override controls, incomplete-document queueing, bulk transfer, inactive-account blocking, period queue reset, normal generation payloads, success warnings, and retained Billing details editing. No production data was changed.

### Limitations, rollback, and next work

Requirements can remain incomplete after listing: staff must follow up through the existing document review workflow. This change does not represent approval of those documents or alter grant amounts. Tests use synthetic records and database facades; hosted authenticated workflows and real-database concurrency are not verified here. Roll back frontend and backend together to restore per-scholar overrides; retain any lists already generated rather than deleting history. Release both components together and perform the checklist with synthetic/test scholars. A future incomplete-requirements filter could simplify follow-up if staff request it.

## 2026-10-12 - Fix Announcement QA and Add Explicit Post Now

### TL;DR
- Added Post Now, Save Draft and Schedule; Post Now immediately publishes new/draft/scheduled notices and clears future publishing dates while retaining audience/priority and validating expiry.
- Fixed urgent notice visibility/selection, stale edit overwrites, expired archival, applicant load failures, server image-size mismatch and misleading published counts; dates now explicitly use PHT/UTC+8.
- Existing notices/history, permissions, public image/private-document separation and list-generation scope retained; no schema/migration, environment or dependency change.
- Validation passed: 241 backend checks/one existing database skip and 72 frontend checks; lint/build and synthetic browser action/conflict/archive/portal/timezone/mobile checks passed. Deployment authorized; publication evidence is tracked in the matching deployment entry.

### Objective and previous/new behavior
Resolve ANN-01–ANN-08 and the user's missing immediate-post action. Previously publication was hidden behind a status selector; priority sorting operated only after a newest-50 cap, personal scholar updates hid general notices, updates overwrote without a revision, historic expiry validation rejected some archives, applicant announcement errors looked empty, raw/encoded image caps differed, published counts claimed visibility and schedule inputs depended on browser timezone.

The management editor now provides explicit Post Now, Save Draft and Schedule plus Save changes for existing records. Actions validate required title/content; Schedule requires a publish date. Post Now sends action post-now, which the server treats as authoritative published status with publish_at=null and a fresh published_at. It rejects expired immediate posts rather than silently removing expiry. Audience, priority, image and link remain part of validated payloads. Confirmation requires a returned announcement ID/revision; unconfirmed failures keep editor/input and do not automatically replay writes. Existing-edit Enter submission selects Save changes rather than Draft. Footer actions wrap on small screens.

### Roles, implementation and data flow
Existing announcement-authorized CAO staff use management; applicant/scholar readers retain audience filtering. latestPriorityAnnouncement queries eligible urgent, then high, then normal notices, each ordered by publication/update/ID, before limiting to one record; recency no longer hides an older urgent record. The scheduler remains request-triggered and portal polling remains five minutes. Scholar portals show a separate CAO announcement card when a personal update exists, retaining both messages/images/links.

Updates require updatedAt. A preliminary check avoids unnecessary uploads for already stale forms; a Serializable transaction conditionally updates that exact revision, increments updated_at monotonically and reads the saved record. Zero matches/serialization conflicts return 409. Rejected edits retain unsaved input and offer an explicit Reload saved version action, labeled as replacing unsaved edits. A newly uploaded update candidate is removed on rejected/failed updates; existing image replacement/removal cleanup remains after commit. Create-upload failure compensation is not expanded by this fix.

Expiry validation permits draft/archive historical records and uses the original publication window for existing notices. Unchanged editor publish/expiry inputs retain their original serialized timestamp precision rather than truncating them to minute-level fields. New immediate publications require valid future expiry. Dates are entered/formatted as Philippine Standard Time, converting only at the UI/API boundary; stored UTC timestamps are not rewritten. Published records replaces the misleading Currently visible metric; Expired badges/filter distinguish expired published rows without changing stored history status.

Applicant announcement reads now distinguish failures from empty success, retain a last-loaded notice with stale guidance and offer Retry announcements. The existing expiry timer, gate, role controls and other portal data flows remain. Image data is decoded before enforcing the same 3 MiB cap as the frontend; supported JPEG/PNG/WEBP/GIF MIME types and declared/data-URL agreement are checked before storage. Existing Facebook HTTPS host/scheme validation remains.

### Changed files/areas and impacts
Changed applicationController, AnnouncementsManagement, ApplicantDashboard, ScholarDashboard and admin styles; added announcementPolicy service and announcementTime utility. Added backend announcementIntegration and frontend announcementTime tests. Added the dated announcement acceptance checklist and updated report/fix register/both change logs.

- **API:** create/update accept optional action post-now; update requires updatedAt and returns 400 for missing revision, 409 for conflicts. Matching frontend/backend required; stale clients must reload. Latest selection keeps its response shape/audience/expiry contract. No new endpoint or permission expansion.
- **Database:** no schema, migration, seed, conversion/deletion of notice records or production queries during validation. Existing updated_at supports revision control; UTC date storage retained. Conflict uploads may be cleaned up through the existing public storage token, never private documents.
- **Configuration/dependencies:** no new package, environment value, provider build/port or hosting setting. Existing Blob and mail systems unchanged.
- **Security/privacy:** server validates byte limits and MIME agreement; this is not magic-byte/malicious-image scanning. Gate/auth/section/rate-limit controls retained; no real account, token, personal document or live notice used in tests. Facebook validation does not establish CAO page ownership.
- **Accessibility:** explicit named native actions, error alert/reload guidance, clear date zone and wrapping footer; sampled 390px page has no horizontal overflow. No full accessibility certification.
- **Deployment:** user authorized matching frontend/backend publication via existing main/Hostinger pipeline; no new migration. Deployment evidence is recorded separately below; local test success is not hosted acceptance.
- **Product scope:** personal list notifications retained unchanged; general announcement separation does not extend into fund release. Legacy payout retirement, historical data and operational logs remain as before.

### Validation and results
Root npm test passed 241 backend checks with one existing opt-in database migration skip, plus 72 frontend checks (313 passes). Backend cases cover due schedule/audience/expiry, normal draft/edit and invalid fields, local route permissions, >50 priority regression, expired archival, new/scheduled Post Now, stale/competing edit CAS, missing revisions/expired immediate post, exact 3 MiB boundaries/MIME mismatch and conflict upload compensation. Frontend time/display regressions passed; final frontend suite rerun after unchanged-date precision handling also passed. Lint/build/whitespace passed; existing large ExcelJS chunk warning remains and 11 route fallbacks generated.

Synthetic Chromium in Manila/UTC browser contexts verifies identical PHT conversion, Schedule validation, Post Now for new/existing records, audience/priority preservation, revision payload/conflict/input retention/manual reload, archival preserving original expiry and 390px wrapping. Applicant failed-load/manual recovery and separate urgent scholar notice beside a read personal update passed; completed runs have no page errors. Initial test fixture auth/environment setup and generated Python/select/capitalization expectations were corrected; no real service/storage mutation occurred. A scoped edit initially affected the profile fetch branch; it was corrected so only announcement reads use the new error handling before final checks.

### Limitations, rollback and recommended next work
No authenticated hosted acceptance, actual PostgreSQL competing-edit execution, real public Blob upload or full accessibility/security/performance test was performed. Five-minute polling/request-triggered scheduling remain; one general notice per audience is selected by priority, not a feed. ## 2026-10-12 - Fix Six Examination Process Boundary Gaps

### TL;DR
- Scholarship acceptance now requires the exact reviewed application, primary period, exam, result and revision; validation and scholar/decision/requirements writes share a Serializable transaction.
- Current applicant/result views no longer substitute an older examination result; accepted scholars retain their referenced historical result. Rejected/declined/withdrawn/unknown states cannot enter or submit examinations.
- Paper review shares primary-period selection with scheduling/online workflows; expired unsubmitted attempts show Attempt expired and CAO guidance without a start action or invented score.
- Validation passed: 231 backend checks, one existing database skip, 70 frontend checks, lint/build and six synthetic browser runs. Local only; no migration, data conversion or deployment. Matching frontend/backend release required.

### Objective and previous/new behavior
Resolve EXAM-01 through EXAM-06 from the dated beginning-to-end review. Previously acceptance read an unbound latest result before its write transaction, allowing stale or historical decisions; online submission excluded only Withdrawn and could overwrite Rejected; question access lacked application-state validation; paper mutations chose the newest active period rather than the primary; expired attempts still advertised access and For review.

Acceptance requests now include applicationId, academicPeriodId, examId, resultId and updatedAt alongside reviewReason. The controller rereads the active primary/fallback period, exact result, latest application, applicant, existing scholar, exam and slot within a Serializable transaction. It checks the supplied revision, current year/municipality/assignment, current schedule identity, publication and passing state before evaluating eligibility and writing. The transaction writes scholar activation, immutable eligibility decision and requirements together. Existing result correction/publication already use Serializable isolation; overlapping incompatible decisions must abort, and P2034/P2002 return a clear 409/reload rather than automatic replay. Ordinary repeat acceptance of the same accepted record remains idempotent. Existing eligibility override reasons, route roles/sections and post-commit approval mail remain.

### Roles, implementation and data flow
CAO staff use the existing Results UI, which sends all exact review identifiers loaded with the result. Missing review fields return 400; stale/context/serialization conflicts return 409 and require fresh review. Portal/staff current examination projections use the current municipal schedule's result instead of the latest all-year result. Active scholars use scholar_accounts.result_id to retain their accepted result; priority accounts without a result remain accepted. Historical result rows are retained, not converted or deleted; existing all-record summary aggregates are unchanged.

The shared examinationEligibility helper allows only Pending, Applied, Submitted, For review, Examined and Passed_Exam application-stage states (case-normalized). Online question access checks the latest application and current/nondeleted applicant before starting time/exposing questions. Paper record/correct/publish and online submission share the application-state rule. Submission rereads the exact latest application inside its transaction, updates that ID only while its status still matches, and requires exactly one changed row; unavailable/conflicting writes roll back the result and send no receipt. Existing current-year/legacy-default applicant targeting is preserved; this is not authorization to reuse a prior year's exam.

The academicPeriod helper centralizes active-primary-first selection with the existing deterministic active fallback. Paper result mutations now use this selector too. The online attempt-state helper distinguishes not-started, active, expired and unavailable started attempts. The shared access predicate denies expired/incomplete attempts or unavailable applications. Progress/guidance and the frontend summary show Attempt expired with contact-CAO instructions; completed results, accepted scholars and terminal decisions retain precedence. Question loading preserves its specific 410 expired-attempt response. Expiry does not reset time, auto-submit answers, create a zero result or declare a failed examination.

### Changed areas and impacts
Changed applicationController, examinationResultController, examinationAccess, examinationProgress and applicantGuidance. Added academicPeriod, examinationEligibility and examinationAttemptState services. Updated ResultsManagement and applicantExamination summary utility; extended backend examination integration/result/access/progress tests, added academicPeriod tests and extended frontend summary tests. Updated both change logs, fix register and the examination review's current fix status. Prior QA-11 and verification documentation edits remain local and are not deployed.

- **API:** acceptance body requires the five exact review fields; older clients must reload/use the matching frontend. Applicant/staff examination projections now use current assignments; management adds applicationId/academicPeriodId and progress adds attemptExpired. Expired/unavailable access is denied. No endpoint, role or section permission additions.
- **Database:** no schema/migration, seed, repair, deadline reset, historical conversion/deletion or production query. Acceptance now uses Serializable isolation; shared exact-application guards protect writes. Existing unique slot/result and scholar constraints retained.
- **Configuration/dependencies:** no environment values, packages, timeouts, configured bank keys, schedule dates, global delivery settings or thresholds changed.
- **Security/privacy:** no real applicant records, passwords, tokens or private files used in validation/documentation. Server checks remain authoritative; unpublished score privacy and tester gate unchanged. No expansion of staff access.
- **Accessibility:** existing native controls retained; expired status has clear text and no examination link, sampled 390px layout has no horizontal overflow. No full-app accessibility claim.
- **Deployment:** local only; deploy matching frontend/backend, with no new migration, then refresh old tabs. This task did not push or deploy.
- **Product scope:** scholarship decision remains separate from examination pass/publication. Workflow still ends at official payroll-list generation. Legacy payout routes remain disabled; historical payment data and unrelated retained legacy interfaces are unchanged. Operational logs remain system records, not monetary audits.

### Validation and results
Root npm test passed 231 backend checks, one existing opt-in school catalog database migration skip, and 70 frontend checks (301 passes; zero failures). New regressions exercise transaction reads/writes/revision/context, corrected-result rejection, historical/mismatched exam/application/period rejection, exact review success/repeat, terminal states, override reasons, rollback/serialization feedback, withdrawn question access, zero-row exact submission rollback, current projection and expired guidance, multiple-active-period paper record/correct/publish and frontend expired-card precedence. Existing score privacy, online grading/version/deadline/draft, list-processing and permission checks remain green.

Frontend lint/build and whitespace checks passed; build generated all 11 route fallbacks and retained the existing large ExcelJS chunk warning. Six synthetic Chromium runs passed: existing paper entry/correction/publication/privacy; objective bank correction; persisted timer/expiry; same-browser answer/draft cleanup; new SuperAdmin paper-through-acceptance UI with captured exact review body; expired applicant status/guidance without a start link at 390px. Final runs had no page errors in checked flows. Initial browser checks exposed the still-For-review frontend summary, which was corrected and regression-tested; a SuperAdmin navigation fixture required a valid applicant-directory payload and was corrected without changing that directory. One initial backend expectation was updated to supply the new exact review contract so it continued checking publication privacy.

### Limitations, rollback and recommended next work
Synthetic transaction facades test controller use, rollback and deterministic interleavings; real PostgreSQL SSI/concurrent correction/acceptance behavior still requires controlled staging verification. No authenticated hosted acceptance/private provider inspection or real mail/exam/scholar write performed. The original review's additional no-show, global-setting interruption and schedule-midnight incident policies are not changed by this fix. Existing all-record aggregate counters remain historical aggregates; current exam rows do not reuse older results. Existing post-commit mail behavior remains; delivery health is separate from transaction integrity.

Rollback must restore matching frontend/backend contracts together and requires no database rollback; doing so restores the reviewed guard weaknesses. Preserve historical results/decisions and additive attempt fields. Next: deploy when requested, refresh tabs, confirm both Hostinger builds, then run dedicated paper/online workflows and acceptance/competing-correction scenarios in staging followed by controlled authenticated hosted tests. ## 2026-10-12 - QA-10: Clear Connection Failures and Preserve Unconfirmed Actions

### TL;DR
- Supported API failures now show plain recovery guidance for unreachable services, timeouts, unreadable responses and HTTP 5xx; validation, permission and conflict messages remain available.
- Failed loads no longer announce empty queues or zero coverage in affected admin/portal views; existing data can remain visible with an error, and reports are withheld until a complete successful load.
- Failed writes explain that completion is unconfirmed without automatic replay. Exam answers and form values remain; examination success requires a recorded receipt, and failed schedule loading cannot trigger cached schedule autosaving.
- Validation passed: 216 backend checks with one existing opt-in database skip, 69 frontend checks, lint/build and synthetic browser failure/retry checks. Local only; not deployed. No backend, schema or configuration change.

### Objective and previous/new behavior
Finish QA-10 beyond the already deployed tester-gate recovery. Browser transport/JSON errors such as Failed to fetch and unreadable proxy replies previously reached many views directly. Some response parsing catches replaced failures with empty objects, permitting empty-state or success messages. Several directories showed No records after a failed request, Reports could infer zero scholarship coverage without a completed load, and schedule loading set the autosave-ready flag even when the initial request failed.

The existing API fetch wrapper now applies shared failure handling to supported API requests, with read versus write recovery wording. Read failures suggest checking connectivity and using Retry or refresh. Write failures explicitly state that completion could not be confirmed and advise checking the affected record before repeating. Application submission advises retaining the form and contacting CAO before resubmitting; examination submission retains its answers and deadline guidance; sign-in offers sign-in retry. No mutation is automatically replayed.

### Roles, implementation and data flow
Applicants, scholars and CAO staff receive consistent connection guidance through existing error panels. The apiFailure service converts fetch/body TypeError and JSON SyntaxError failures, preserves intentional AbortError cancellation, and preserves TimeoutError identity for existing deadline handling. HTTP 5xx becomes a safe service-unavailable error without exposing a proxy body or server detail. Ordinary successful structured JSON passes through; null/scalar JSON is rejected as unreadable. Native blob/text readers preserve successful data and normalize body transport errors. Ordinary HTTP 400/401/403/409/410/429 responses retain their payloads and status, so field validation, session handling, access controls, retired-route messages and conflict behavior remain available.

The wrapper retains tester-token injection and access-challenge handling. Tester-gate URLs remain under their existing dedicated ten-second request/deadline/error handling; unrelated URLs are untouched. Removed swallowed JSON failures from affected API consumers. Existing auth-session and health-panel fallback parsing is retained because these callers already treat an absent payload conservatively rather than presenting a save success.

Admin overview, staff, activity logs, document review, catalogs, announcements, scholars, results and Payroll suppress affected empty conclusions and mark unavailable metrics/counts. Overview distinguishes unavailable/last-loaded data. Reports commit scholar and lifecycle data together, withhold metrics/coverage until a complete successful load, and disable export when the report is unavailable. Scholar record sections stay hidden until loaded; auxiliary announcement/notification errors preserve earlier data and offer update retry. Applicant portal retry retains its existing error-state flow.

Examination loading no longer swallows bad JSON; successful submission requires receipt.recorded === true before displaying success and clearing its draft. Unconfirmed responses leave answers/modal available. Schedule readiness is set only after a successful initial schedule load, preventing failed initial loading from enabling automatic persistence of local defaults. Assigned-applicant errors are explicit rather than being replaced by an empty list. Sign-in validates its required token/role fields before handing off an authenticated session. Existing examination timing, grading, results privacy and local draft boundaries remain intact.

### Changed files/areas and impacts
Added frontend/src/services/apiFailure.js and frontend/tests/apiFailure.test.js; updated the existing services/api.js fetch wrapper. Updated error/parsing/loading displays in Dashboard, ReportsManagement, ScholarDashboard, ApplicantDashboard, BillingPayrollManagement, ScholarsManagement, ResultsManagement, StaffManagement, ActivityLogsManagement, DocumentReviewManagement, SchoolCatalogManagement, AnnouncementsManagement, ExamPage, PasswordRecoveryPage and the LoginForm/ApplicationForm components. Updated both change logs and QA fix register.

- **API:** frontend request/body failure handling changes; no backend endpoints, server response contracts or authorization changes. HTTP 5xx now enters existing client error paths immediately. Examination receipt and sign-in required fields are checked before client success.
- **Database:** no schema change, migration, data repair, deletion, seed or production query. Preventing autosave after a failed initial schedule load avoids unintended writes from an unverified local state.
- **Configuration/dependencies:** no environment-variable, hosting, package or dependency changes. Existing timeouts and polling intervals remain.
- **Security/privacy:** existing tester gate, token injection, authentication and section checks retained. Server/proxy internals are not shown for 5xx failures; verification uses synthetic users/records only. Error causes remain available for local diagnostics rather than being rendered as messages.

## 2026-10-11 - QA-07: Commit Online Results and Application Status Together

### TL;DR
- Online submission now commits the score and application status as one transaction; a failed status write rolls back the score.
- Applicants with no matching non-withdrawn application receive a conflict response without a saved result or receipt email.
- Existing slot uniqueness prevents duplicate scores; receipt delivery follows commit and unpublished scores remain private.
- Root tests passed: 209 backend checks with one existing opt-in database skip, plus 56 frontend checks. Release `6ef9bb7` pushed through the authorized main/Hostinger pipeline; frontend/API healthy and user confirmed Hostinger backend deployment success. No migration is required.

### Objective and previous/new behavior
Resolve QA-07's partial-save risk for applicants submitting an online examination. Previously the result was inserted before a separate application-status update. A failed second write could leave a saved score with an unchanged status, and retry would then report an already submitted examination. Both writes now use the same interactive Prisma transaction. An update affecting zero non-withdrawn applications throws a conflict and rolls back the insert. Existing applicant-wide non-withdrawn status selection is retained; this change does not redesign application history or repair historical partial writes.

### Roles, implementation and data flow
Applicant submissions still validate online availability, attendance, the original question version, answer grading and the persisted 45-minute deadline before writing. The transaction client creates the result and advances matching application submissions to Examined. Any failure aborts both writes. The existing application database unique constraint on results.exam_slot_id provides one winner for simultaneous submissions; the losing request receives HTTP 409. Only after commit does the controller look up the control number and send the existing receipt notification. CAO result review/publication, paper score entry and scholarship acceptance retain their existing workflows. Changed backend/controllers/applicationController.js and backend/tests/examinationIntegration.test.js, both change logs and docs/qa-fix-register.md.

### Impacts
- **API:** successful HTTP 201 receipt and unpublished-score privacy are retained. Missing/withdrawn application updates now return HTTP 409 with Contact CAO guidance; write failures remain HTTP 500 and duplicates HTTP 409.
- **Database:** transactional write boundary added using existing tables and uniqueness. No schema change, migration, historical result rewrite, seed or production data repair.
- **Configuration/deployment:** no environment-variable or frontend change. Deploy backend through existing main-branch Hostinger auto-build; no new migration. Public health does not identify the deployed backend revision.
- **Security/privacy:** existing authorization, signed ticket/version checks and deadline rules retained. No new access or personal data exposure; synthetic fixtures only in tests.
- **Accessibility:** no visual/interface change; existing submission errors display the new conflict message through current handling.
- **Product scope:** workflow still ends at official payroll-list generation. Legacy payment/release functionality is retained unchanged outside approved scope; no monetary audit or release flow added.

### Validation, limitations, rollback and next work
Root npm test passed 209 backend checks, one existing opt-in real-database test skipped, and 56 frontend checks. Four additional controller integration tests cover commit-before-notification, forced status-write failure with rollback and successful retry, withdrawn/missing applications, and simultaneous/duplicate submissions with a single receipt. Tests use a serialized rollback-capable in-memory transaction facade and exercise existing HTTP integrations; they do not prove hosted PostgreSQL isolation or simulate real provider failures. The application Prisma schema already declares results.exam_slot_id unique. No frontend build is required for this backend-only change. Whitespace and remote main baseline checks passed before release. Push advanced main from `21bfa85` to `6ef9bb7`. Public frontend returned HTTP 200 and API health returned healthy with database connected. The user confirmed Hostinger backend deployment success for `6ef9bb7`; a subsequent public API check returned healthy with database connected. Provider success is user-reported; build logs and authenticated hosted submission were not independently inspected.

No existing inconsistent records are automatically repaired. Receipt delivery is outside the database transaction; a later notification/account lookup failure can occur after a committed submission, as before. Concurrency protection assumes the deployed application's existing unique constraint. Roll back the controller/test change without database rollback, understanding that rollback restores the partial-write risk. Next: use a dedicated authorized test attempt for hosted acceptance; proceed separately to QA-09 legacy route review.

## 2026-10-11 - QA-05: Bound Tester Verification and Allow Recovery

### TL;DR
- Tester status and unlock requests now have a 10-second deadline covering response headers and JSON body reading, preventing indefinite verification spinners.
- Status failure offers Retry verification; unlock failure restores usable controls and preserves the entered code for retry. Access remains locked until a valid authorized response is received.
- Pending requests are cancelled on unmount, newer checks and expired-session events; stale responses cannot authorize the gate. No backend, database or protected-code configuration changes.
- All 56 frontend tests, lint/build and synthetic Chromium timeout/retry/fail-closed/mobile checks passed. Local only; QA-04 same-browser recovery is retained as requested and neither local fix is deployed yet.

### Objective and previous/new behavior
Resolve QA-05's hanging invitation-only checkpoint. Previously a pending status/unlock fetch or stalled JSON response could leave all users waiting without a time limit. Status already had a Retry control for ordinary failures, but a hang never reached it. Now both requests abort after 10 seconds and show connection/retry guidance. Malformed responses produce readable errors; ambiguous authorization and required unlock responses lacking a token remain locked. A failed unlock leaves the code in component memory and re-enables the form; it does not require repeating unrelated account credentials.

### Affected roles, implementation and data flow
All visitors pass through the tester gate before account sign-in. A shared request helper attaches an AbortController and retains its timeout through body parsing. The gate stores the current controller in a ref, aborts older requests, and ignores completions that no longer belong to the active request. Session-expiry events cancel pending unlocks, clear the code and restore the locked form. Unmount cancels pending work. Requests are manually retried rather than automatically looping against the server's existing rate limiter. Inputs are disabled while unlock is pending and duplicate submits are ignored.

### Files and system areas
`frontend/src/components/SiteAccessGate.jsx`, `frontend/src/services/siteAccessRequest.js`, timeout/request tests, both change logs and the local QA report status. The existing tester-token header installation, backend gate enforcement, roles, exam grading/timing and browser answer recovery remain unchanged.

### Impact assessment
- **API/database:** no endpoint, payload, backend validation, schema, migration or production data changes. Existing status/unlock routes and session tokens are reused.
