An independent Python standard-library check validated ZIP integrity and parsed every XML/relationship part of a synthetic 80-record DOCX, verifying 81 seven-cell rows including the repeatable header. No production data or attendance writes were used. Backend tests were not rerun for this frontend-only export-format change.

## 2026-10-18 - Applicant eligibility-declaration filter

**TL;DR**
- Applicants directory now includes Eligibility criteria with all seven choices from the application form, plus Any declared criterion and No criteria declared.
- It combines with search/status/location/school-year filters, resets pagination, participates in Clear filters and affects existing filtered CSV rows.
- Filtering uses applicant declarations only; proof approval, priority, eligibility, family constraints and Scholar acceptance are unchanged.
- All 154 frontend tests, lint/build and whitespace checks passed; user has now requested deployment.

### Objective and previous/new behavior
Make the application form's eligibility declarations usable for staff directory filtering. Previously staff could read declarations in an applicant drawer but could not filter the directory by them. Added one labelled dropdown covering Graduated Valedictorian or Highest Honors, Academic Contest Champion/1st Placer, ALS Passer, PWD, Child of PWD, Solo Parent and Indigenous Group. All eligibility criteria keeps every row otherwise matching the existing filters. Any declared criterion matches at least one affirmative declaration; No criteria declared means no known affirmative declaration, not a determination that an applicant is ineligible. The one-scholar-per-family acknowledgement is intentionally not treated as a priority declaration.

### Roles, workflow, implementation and data flow
Existing authorized Applicants staff use data already supplied by applicants/management. matchesApplicantEligibility reads the seven existing eligibility keys, accepting Yes case-insensitively/trimmed and legacy boolean true, while rejecting false/No/missing/other truthy values. Child-of-PWD does not imply the applicant has PWD status. The chosen criterion is ANDed with the directory's existing filters; changing it resets page one, active-filter detection includes it and Clear filters resets it to all. The existing sortedApplicants pipeline continues to drive visible records and CSV exports; no new export columns or applicant fields are added. Six toolbar fields use a three-column layout on wide screens and a stacked phone layout.

### Files and system impacts
Dashboard.jsx ApplicantsManagement section; components/ApplicantEligibilityFilter.jsx; utils/applicantEligibilityFilter.js; styles/applicant-eligibility-filter.css; tests/applicantEligibilityFilter.test.js; required logs. API/backend/database/schema/migration/configuration: no impact. Security/privacy: existing authentication and staff section permissions remain; potentially sensitive declarations were already present in the authorized directory response and drawer, with no new fetch, storage or disclosure scope. No declaration, proof, priority score, application status or family-policy mutation occurs. Accessibility: native labelled select, explicit declaration-not-proof guidance via aria-describedby, existing focus handling and responsive touch targets. Deployment: user requested publication through the existing main-branch hosting pipeline, without infrastructure changes. Legacy payment-oriented areas are untouched and retained outside the approved payroll-list-generation boundary.

### Validation
Tests cover all seven independent categories, Yes/boolean normalization and negative/missing/malformed values, all/any/none behavior, family acknowledgement exclusion, distinction between PWD and child-of-PWD, declaration versus proof approval, rendered choices/selected state/guidance and callback, existing-filter intersection, pagination reset/Clear filters, and filtered CSV data flow. Final suite/lint/build output follows below. No production accounts or records were accessed or modified. Backend tests were not rerun for this frontend-only filter.

### Limitations, rollback and next work
This is a single-criterion selector, not a multi-criterion AND/OR query builder. Missing legacy declarations fall under No criteria declared; they are not inferred as verified negative responses. Summary metric cards retain their existing overall counts; directory/export rows reflect the active filters. Browser screenshot validation is unavailable in this environment. After rollout, verify filters and CSV with a controlled staff session. Revert these frontend changes to remove the new dropdown without any data rollback.

## 2026-10-18 - Optional first-year Grade 12 report card for initial requirements

**TL;DR**
- Incoming/first-year college applicants can use either an approved COG or Grade 12 report card as initial academic evidence; both are not required.
- CAO uploads initial files individually; applicants/scholars retain private View access. Higher-year and continuing COG requirements are unchanged.
- Existing versioned document JSON storage is reused; no migration, credentials or new upload permissions.
- Backend 388 tests passed (one database test skipped), frontend 157 passed; lint, build and whitespace checks passed. User requested deployment through the existing hosting pipeline.

### Objective and behavior
Allow incoming/first-year students without registrar-issued college grades to use their Grade 12 report card in the initial CAO intake. Previously initial verification always required COG. Now an approved COG OR report card satisfies the initial academic-document group for a confirmed first-year entry. The report card remains optional when COG exists; COG is not additionally required when the report card is approved. All other required documents, private-school tuition receipts, and posted/locked Passer List safeguards remain unchanged. Missing, pending or rejected evidence cannot complete the group. Higher-year or unknown entry-year records still require COG. Continuing submissions still require college grades and cannot substitute a report card.

### Roles, implementation and data flow
The original application school-plan incoming year controls eligibility, not a later scholar year. Backend initialAcademicEvidence recognizes explicit first-year/incoming-first-year values. Initial requirement definitions add report_card; staff uploads validate the entry year before storage and again within transactional updates. Checklist metadata marks COG/report card as alternatives; common initial approval evaluates either approved file only for eligible entries. Continuing access, acceptance, certification/payroll-list readiness use that shared rule. Staff phone capture includes report cards only for qualifying applications. Private storage, per-document approval/version history and authenticated owner/staff streaming are reused. Report cards are never aliased to continuing grades. Scholar progress counts the academic group once, including when both files exist. Existing report-card files remain viewable after entry-year metadata changes but do not waive higher-year COG. Initial uploads remain CAO-owned, not applicant self-service.

### Files and system areas
Backend: initialAcademicEvidence helper; requirementWaves, continuingSchedule, documentReview, passerIntake services; application, passer-list, lifecycle-report, phone-capture controllers and tests. Frontend: initialAcademicEvidence helper, InitialRequirementCapture, InitialVerificationDocuments and styles, ApplicantDashboard, ScholarDashboard, PhoneCapturePage and tests. Both required logs updated; prior deployment observations retained.

### API, data, security and deployment impacts
API: additive initial report_card key, optional/alternative-group metadata and entry-year response field; existing upload/view endpoints reused. Database: no schema or migration, existing JSON/waves store the added document. Configuration: no new environment variables/settings. Security/privacy: existing staff-only initial uploads, active-account, period, ownership, private-file access and concurrency protections retained; no public document URLs or real records in tests. Accessibility: labeled controls, textual guidance/status and existing accessible View buttons retained; note wraps responsively. Deployment: commit/push using the existing connected frontend/backend hosting pipeline; no production record mutations during validation. Product scope still ends at official payroll-list generation. Legacy payment-oriented functionality is retained unchanged, not extended into release, claims, reconciliation or monetary audit.

### Validation
Full safe runner: backend 388 passed, zero failures, one database-dependent migration test skipped; frontend 157 passed, zero failures. Added tests cover first-year recognition, either-document approval, missing/pending/rejected evidence, higher/unknown-year restrictions, private tuition requirements, optional checklist metadata, private preview, staff upload restrictions, separate continuing COG and one-group progress counts. Existing document/access regressions pass. ESLint, production frontend build and git diff --check passed; existing large-chunk build advisory is non-fatal. Synthetic tests do not mutate production. Browser visual and authenticated production end-to-end tests are not performed here.

### Limitations, rollback and next work
Only explicit first-year entry metadata activates the alternative; incorrect source data should be corrected rather than bypassed. Recommended live smoke test: use a test first-year applicant with other initial files approved and report card without COG, verify initial acceptance readiness, both document View paths and separate continuing COG. Rollback by reverting the release, preserving all stored report-card files. Older code will not recognize report-card-only approval and would require COG again; no destructive cleanup is appropriate.

## 2026-10-18 - Clickable administrative summary cards and record modals

**TL;DR**
- Active Scholars and Forfeited Accounts on the main dashboard now open complete searchable, paginated record lists; live operational summary cards in the other staff workspaces use the same read-only modal.
- Covers Applicants, Scholars, Examination Results, Documents, Announcements, Reports, Billing/Certification, Payroll, Staff and Activity Logs. Lists preserve each card's population and count semantics, rather than showing only the current directory page.
- Hidden/unassigned sections remain inaccessible: main detail reads require Dashboard plus Scholars or Examination permission, with server enforcement and disabled UI controls. No workflow decisions or production records are changed.
- Backend 398 tests passed, one database-dependent test skipped; frontend 165 passed. ESLint, production build and whitespace checks passed. Deployment requested through the existing connected hosting pipeline.

### Objective and reason
The client requested that totals explain themselves: clicking Active Scholars should reveal the names behind that number without navigating away. Previously summary cards were non-interactive totals, leaving staff to locate the equivalent directory/filter manually. The change provides a consistent record drill-down for live administrative summary cards, while retaining the original card layout and section permissions.

### Previous and new behavior, roles and workflows
Main Dashboard: clicking Active Scholars opens active scholarship-account records with names, scholar IDs and municipality; Forfeited Accounts opens forfeited examination-slot records with names and examination references. The latter intentionally preserves one record per forfeited slot, including repeat people, because that is the existing total's definition. Cards requiring a hidden/unassigned directory are disabled rather than granting access through Dashboard.
Applicants: Total Applicants shows people, Scheduled for Exam uses the exact current-year/legacy-year municipality-or-persisted-slot membership, and Exam Completed/Passed Applicants show examination result records, preserving multiple results per person when present. Scholars shows total/active/document-complete/review memberships. Examination Results shows total/review/scored/passed/failed memberships. Document Reviews shows pending/approved/rejected/all upload records. Announcements preserves stored publication states, including expired published records. Staff shows total/active/inactive/active provincial-admin populations. Reports shows the selected school-year active/graduating scholars and actual zero-coverage municipalities or low/zero-coverage barangays, independent of other directory filters.
Certification/Payroll summary cards show current-period, matching-route scholar records at their existing list-preparation stage. Generated Lists retains its existing meaning of listed scholar records, not a fabricated batch count. The fixed Grant (PHP) card opens an explanation of the configured PHP 5,000 tuition support with the applicable private-route scholar records; the currency amount is not described as a record count or payment release. Activity Logs opens the full paginated event subset for Today, Last 7 days, Sign-ins or Admin actions, not merely the currently loaded log page.
All detail views are read-only: no record mutation, acceptance, document approval, notification, export, release or access-role change is triggered. Ordinary section authentication remains authoritative. Applicants/scholars do not receive administrative modal endpoints.

### Implementation and data flow
A shared MetricDetailsCard preserves the existing article/styles and adds a full-card native button with dialog semantics. The portal-mounted native dialog supplies browser focus containment, Escape dismissal, initial search focus, focus restoration, background scroll locking, a responsive scrollable table, 25-record pages, safe text rendering, search, loading/empty/error states and Retry. Remote reads are debounced for search, cancellable on changes/close, protected against stale-request rendering and bounded by a 20-second timeout. Network/response parsing failures show safe recovery messages.
Main Dashboard GET /dashboard/metrics/:metric supports only activeScholars/forfeitedAccounts, validates page/search, limits each page to 25, selects minimal fields and suppresses identities for unavailable/deleted applicant rows. The existing total population is retained even when a linked applicant is unavailable. Search uses name/municipality tokens and filters the corresponding count and page; page bounds are clamped if data changes. Dashboard summary supplies additive metricAccess flags. Both reads use private/no-store responses. The route requires authentication, an operational staff role, Dashboard access and the corresponding underlying section permission.
Applicant management adds minimal metricRecords memberships using existing authorized datasets. The scheduling service exposes IDs from the same algorithm its count already uses, avoiding divergent membership. Activity Logs adds a validated metric filter using the exact existing Philippine-day/week, USER_LOGIN and admin-actor predicates. Other sections reuse their already authorized in-memory records and matching summary predicates; unrelated directory filters do not silently narrow the total. Search is limited to displayed columns. No document contents or private file URLs are added to the modal API.

### Files and system areas changed
Backend: dashboardDetailsController (new); applicationController, activityController, applicationRoutes; examAssignments service; dashboardDetails tests (new) and examination integration regression. Frontend: MetricDetailsCard, metricDetails helper and modal CSS (new); Dashboard, ScholarsManagement, ResultsManagement, BillingPayrollManagement, DocumentReviewManagement, StaffManagement, AnnouncementsManagement, ReportsManagement and ActivityLogsManagement; metricDetails regressions (new). Required change logs updated and prior release observations retained.

### API, database, configuration, security, privacy, accessibility and deployment impact
API: additive authenticated dashboard detail endpoint, summary access flags and applicant metricRecords; optional validated activity metric query. Existing summary counts and mutation contracts are unchanged. Database: read-only queries and existing datasets, no schema/data migration. Configuration: no new settings, dependencies, secrets or environment variables. Security/privacy: existing role and section access retained; extra directory permission required for dashboard drill-down; minimal selected identity fields, no public personal data, private/no-store responses, no sensitive request bodies or file data. Existing staff/log endpoints keep their prior restrictions. Accessibility: native keyboard-operable buttons/dialog, labelled title/description/search, focus containment/restoration, Escape/Close actions, focus outlines, status/alert feedback, horizontal table scrolling and mobile viewport sizing. Deployment: publish frontend/backend via existing main-branch connected hosting; no production record mutations are needed for verification. Product scope remains CAO official payroll-list generation. Legacy payment-oriented fields/code are retained unchanged outside scope; the new modals describe operational records and list preparation, not payment claims, fund release, reconciliation or monetary audits.

### Validation and results
Full safe regression runner: backend 398 passed, zero failures, one database-dependent migration test intentionally skipped; frontend 165 passed, zero failures. Added checks cover real-route authentication, role and combined section permissions (including narrowed Billing access), private cache headers, complete account pagination, repeat forfeiture records, invalid metrics/pages/search, name searches, stale-page clamping, empty/unavailable applicants, summary permission flags, exact applicant result/scheduled cardinality, event metric predicates, native dialog/button markup, escaped record text, 25-row pages, displayed-column search and metric-specific memberships across sections. Existing workflow/security tests remain green. ESLint, production build and git diff --check passed; the existing large-chunk build advisory remains non-fatal. Synthetic facades/local HTTP tests do not access production records. Browser visual interaction and authenticated production end-to-end tests are not claimed.

### Limitations, rollback and recommended next work
These are live operational summary cards, not an expansion of legacy placeholder/template cards or report charts into new workflows. Lists use current authorized data; records can change between a summary refresh and modal opening. Most workspace modals reuse the already-loaded full dataset and update with workspace refresh; Dashboard and Activity Logs read complete server-paginated populations on demand. Name/municipality search is provided for main Dashboard. Exact production backend revision cannot be inferred from a healthy health endpoint alone. Recommended test-account smoke checks: click Active Scholars, search a known test name, traverse pages and close via Escape; compare count/membership with Scholars, inspect Forfeited Accounts and a Passed Applicants card, and repeat with a staff account lacking directory permission. Check responsive dialog layout on mobile. Revert this release to roll back; there are no data writes/migrations to undo. Future scaling can replace in-memory workspace modal datasets with matching server-paginated membership endpoints if directory sizes demand it.

### Deployment observation
Published release 4a1c60a to origin/main through the existing connected hosting pipeline. The live homepage now references index-CnRGUQr5.js; Dashboard-B1_4J0tu.js returns HTTP 200 JavaScript with the dashboard metric endpoint/access flags, native labelled record dialog, searchable/paginated record details and applicant metricRecords integration. Dashboard-I4jxm1Sg.css returns HTTP 200 CSS with the modal and keyboard-focus styles. Public API health returns HTTP 200, healthy with database connected. The new dashboard details URL refuses unauthenticated access with HTTP 401. This confirms public frontend/style rollout, API availability and an authentication boundary, not an authenticated production record interaction or an exact backend revision. ## 2026-10-18 - Phone-first Scholar Portal layout refinements

**TL;DR**

### Objective and previous/new behavior
The user expects most scholars to use phones and requested mobile optimization. Existing responsive rules still left some requirement rows in flex layouts despite a one-column grid declaration; long filenames/actions competed for narrow width, several controls were below comfortable touch size, and notification history was not height-bounded. New scoped mobile rules explicitly use one-column document grids, wrapping action rows and full-width upload affordances. Navigation links let users reach Updates, Requirements and Summary without scrolling the entire page repeatedly. The existing action-first content order and complete announcement text are preserved.

### Roles, workflows, implementation and data flow
Changes apply to Scholar Portal layouts up to 760px with a compact navigation treatment below 400px. A shared native-anchor ScholarMobileNavigation is shown only when application content is available and hidden on desktop; it targets existing Updates, Requirements and Summary sections, making no new API calls or workflow mutations. A last-loaded scholar-mobile stylesheet overrides earlier responsive rules while remaining scoped to the scholar-dashboard root. It refines the header and visible logout, welcome/ID wrapping, next-step action, requirement tabs, document labels/filenames/status/view/upload controls, 16px period selectors, profile fields and toast dismissal. ## 2026-10-18 - Scholar Portal desktop section navigator

**TL;DR**
- Added a desktop left-side section rail inspired by the supplied reference, using Overview, Summary, Next step, Updates and Requirements instead of placeholder labels.
- Current-section highlighting follows scrolling; a dedicated grid column prevents content overlap. Smaller desktops use a compact horizontal strip; mobile quick links remain unchanged.
- Read-only in-page navigation only; no API, database, upload, notification or scholarship-workflow changes.
- Frontend 177 tests passed, plus ESLint, production build and whitespace checks. Release 25134ba deployed; live navigation/CSS and API health verified. Rendered desktop/browser acceptance remains recommended.

### Objective and previous/new behavior
The user requested a desktop navigation treatment like the screenshot's vertical line, branch markers and section labels. Desktop scholars previously had to scroll manually or use the next-step requirement action; mobile already had quick links. The portal now provides five named anchor links with a visible current-section marker. At widths of at least 1024px the rail remains on the left as the page scrolls; widths 761-1023px use a wrapping horizontal strip. It is hidden at phone widths so the existing mobile navigation remains the sole quick-link control there.

### Roles, implementation and data flow
Affects scholars viewing their own portal. ScholarDesktopNavigation mounts only when application content is available, next to the existing main element inside a scoped desktop layout wrapper. Overview and next-step sections gain stable focusable anchor targets; existing summary, updates and requirements targets are reused. Native links preserve keyboard navigation and browser hash behavior without introducing routes or requests. Active tracking measures actual visual section positions through a passive scroll listener and requestAnimationFrame; a ResizeObserver updates tracking when content expands or refreshes. The current section uses aria-current=location. Bottom-of-page handling selects the final section, and listeners/observer/queued frames are cleaned up on unmount. Navigation adds no forced smooth animation and does not collapse or alter document stages.

Legacy payment-oriented functionality is retained unchanged and not extended into fund release, claim tracking, disbursement, reconciliation or monetary auditing.
